facts.fact: Bing Concert Hall is a performing arts building at Stanford University that opened in January 2013.
facts.quote: Bing Concert Hall is a performing arts facility at Stanford University that opened in January 2013.

facts.fact: Its heart is an oval concert hall with 842 seats set in vineyard-style terraces around the stage.
facts.quote: The heart of the building is the oval-shaped concert hall, which has 842 seats arranged in a vineyard style surrounding the stage in terraces.

facts.fact: Every seat is within 75 feet of the conductor, and the centre seats begin at stage level.
facts.quote: All the seats are within 75 feet of the conductor, and the seats in the center section begin at the stage level.

facts.fact: A smaller room, the Bing Studio, sits north of the hall and can be set up for cabaret, club or theatre use.
facts.quote: On the north side of the central concert hall is the smaller Bing Studio, which can be configured to accommodate a variety of performance types, e.g., cabaret, club, and theater.

facts.fact: It was designed by Richard Olcott of Ennead Architects, with acoustics by Yasuhisa Toyota of Nagata Acoustics, who also worked on Walt Disney Concert Hall.
facts.quote: Bing Concert Hall was designed by Richard Olcott of Ennead Architects, with the acoustics done by Yasuhisa Toyota of Nagata Acoustics, who also worked on Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles, California and New World Symphony in Miami Beach, Florida.

facts.fact: Construction finally cost $111.9 million.

facts.fact: The church was designed by Alvar Aalto and completed in 1958.
facts.quote: The church was designed by Alvar Aalto and completed in 1958.

facts.fact: It is said to be Aalto's most original church design, and it is named after the three crosses at the altar.
facts.quote: It is said to be Aalto's most original church design. The church gets its name from the three crosses at the altar.

facts.fact: The church is three halls in a row that sliding walls can separate, so parts can be used for parish activities during the week.
facts.quote: The church consists of three consecutive halls which can be separated by sliding walls; this enables parts of the church to be used for parish activities during the week.

facts.fact: Outside, the church is white with a copper roof.
facts.quote: The exterior of the church is white with a copper roofing.

facts.fact: Docomomo lists it as a significant example of modern architecture in Finland, and it is a nationally significant built heritage site.
facts.quote: Docomomo has listed the church as a significant example of modern architecture in Finland. The Finnish Heritage Agency has also listed it as a nationally significant built heritage site.

facts.fact: In 1998 a Finnish Heritage Agency committee chose it as one of Aalto's five most important buildings.
facts.quote: A committee designated by the Finnish Heritage Agency in 1998 to commemorate the centenary of Aalto's birth selected the church as one of the five most important buildings designed by Aalto.

facts.fact: In July 2026 it was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 12 other Aalto works.
facts.quote: In July 2026, the Church of the Three Crosses, along with 12 other Aalto Works, was designated by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: The stadium was built as the main venue for the 1972 Summer Olympics, at the heart of Munich's Olympic Park.
facts.quote: Situated at the heart of the Olympiapark München in northern Munich, the stadium was built as the main venue for the 1972 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: It was designed by architect Günther Behnisch and engineer Frei Otto, and its lightweight tent construction was considered revolutionary for its time.
facts.quote: Designed by the German architect Günther Behnisch and the engineer Frei Otto, with the assistance of John Argyris, the lightweight tent construction of the Olympiastadion was considered revolutionary for its time.

facts.fact: Its sweeping canopies of acrylic glass, held by steel cables, were the first of their kind on a large scale.
facts.quote: This included large sweeping canopies of acrylic glass stabilized by steel cables that were used for the first time on a large scale.

facts.fact: The roof was meant to echo the Alps and to contrast with the 1936 Berlin Olympics held under the Nazis.
facts.quote: The idea was to imitate the Alps skyline and to set a counterpoint to the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin, held during the Nazi regime.

facts.fact: The transparent canopy was designed to stand for a new, democratic and optimistic West Germany.
facts.quote: The sweeping and transparent canopy was designed to symbolize the new, democratic and optimistic West Germany.

facts.fact: The competition model won over the jury with its landscape and tent roof, matching the Games' theme of human scale, lightness and unity of landscape and nature.
facts.quote: The model convinced with its surrounding landscape architecture and the tent roof construction. Thus, it fulfilled the leitmotif of the games: human scale, lightness, bold elegance and unity of the landscape with nature.

facts.fact: Otto worked out parts of the roof by trial and error with large models, while Andrä and Leonhardt developed it with a CAD program.
facts.quote: Otto developed parts of the roof by means of the trial-and-error principle by making larger models of the roof construction, while Andrä and Leonhardt developed the roof with a CAD program elsewhere.

facts.fact: The Olympic Mountain beside it was made from wartime bomb rubble, shaped as an oval so it could serve as a stadium's seating base.
facts.quote: After the World War II, the debris rubble of the bombing of the city was piled up, from which the Olympic Mountain emerged. This was intentionally created in an oval shape, so that it could be used as a tribune foundation for a stadium.

facts.fact: CaixaForum Madrid is a cultural centre on the Paseo del Prado, in a former power station owned by the foundation "la Caixa".
facts.quote: Located in Paseo del Prado in a former power station, it is owned by the not-for-profit banking foundation "la Caixa".

facts.fact: It opened in 2008 and holds temporary art exhibitions and cultural events.
facts.quote: The art center opened its doors in 2008 and it hosts temporary art exhibitions and cultural events.

facts.fact: It was designed by Herzog & de Meuron and built by Ferrovial between 2001 and 2007.
facts.quote: The cultural center was designed by the Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron and built by Ferrovial between 2001 and 2007.

facts.fact: The building was an old power station from the 1900s called Central del Mediodía.
facts.quote: It was an old power station called Central Del Mediodía, from the 1900s.

facts.fact: Patrick Blanc's vertical garden on the square is also well known.
facts.quote: The Vertical Garden by Patrick Blanc at the square is also well-known.

facts.fact: The National Museum of Roman Art is an archaeology museum in Mérida, Spain, devoted to Roman art.
facts.quote: The National Museum of Roman Art (Spanish: Museo Nacional de Arte Romano; MNAR) is an archaeology museum in Mérida, Spain.

facts.fact: It shows finds from Roman Augusta Emerita, one of Spain's largest archaeological sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.
facts.quote: Devoted to Roman art, it exhibits extensive material from the archaeological ensemble of Mérida (the Roman colony of Augusta Emerita), one of the largest and most extensive archaeological sites in Spain, registered as UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

facts.fact: The museum was refounded as the National Museum of Roman Art in 1975, for the city's 2,000th anniversary.
facts.quote: In 1975, on the occasion of the two thousandth anniversary of the city's foundation, the museum was refounded as the National Museum of Roman Art.

facts.fact: The current building is by Rafael Moneo; work began in 1981.
facts.quote: The current building is a work by Spanish architect Rafael Moneo. Building works started in 1981.

facts.fact: The new building opened on 19 September 1986.
facts.quote: The new premises were unveiled on 19 September 1986.

facts.fact: 122 Leadenhall Street, nicknamed the Cheesegrater, is a 225-metre skyscraper in central London.
facts.quote: 122 Leadenhall Street, also known as the Leadenhall Building, Leadenhall Tower or informally the Cheesegrater, is a 225-metre-tall (738 ft) skyscraper in central London.

facts.fact: It opened in July 2014 and was designed by Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners.
facts.quote: It opened in July 2014 and was designed by Rogers Stirk Harbour + Partners.

facts.fact: The tapered glass façade shows the steel bracing, with a ladder frame stressing the building's height.
facts.quote: The new tower features a tapered glass façade on one side which reveals steel bracings, along with a ladder frame to emphasise the vertical appearance of the building.

facts.fact: Instead of a concrete core, a steel 'Megaframe' engineered by Arup keeps the whole structure stable; it is the world's tallest of its kind.
facts.quote: Unlike other tall buildings, which typically use a concrete core to provide stability, the steel "Megaframe", engineered by Arup, provides stability to the entire structure and is the world's tallest of its kind.

facts.fact: At its base is a 30 m high atrium open to the public, extending the plaza next to it.
facts.quote: The base features a 30m high atrium which is open to the public and extends the adjacent plaza.

facts.fact: The flat side, also glazed, holds the lifts, whose orange counterweights and motors are put on show as at the neighbouring Lloyd's Building.
facts.quote: The flat side of the building is also encased in glass, and houses the mechanical services – in particular the elevator shafts. These have been turned into an architectural feature, similar to the neighbouring Lloyd's Building – they deliberately display the elevator machinery, with bright orange counterweights and elevator motors.

facts.fact: The slanted wedge was meant to lessen its impact on the protected view of St Paul's Cathedral from Fleet Street.
facts.quote: It is hoped that the slanting wedge-shaped design will have less impact on the protected sightline of St Paul's Cathedral when viewed from Fleet Street and the west.

facts.fact: The museum holds the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings and drawings.
facts.quote: The museum contains the largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings and drawings in the world.

facts.fact: The Dutch government commissioned Gerrit Rietveld to design it in 1963.
facts.quote: Design for a Van Gogh Museum was commissioned by the Dutch government in 1963 to Dutch architect and furniture designer Gerrit Rietveld.

facts.fact: Rietveld died a year later, and the building was finished only in 1973, when the museum opened.
facts.quote: Rietveld died a year later, and the building was not completed until 1973, when the museum opened its doors.

facts.fact: The Rietveld building is the main building and holds the permanent collection; it has a rectangular plan and four storeys.
facts.quote: The Rietveld building is the main structure and houses the permanent collection. It has a rectangular floor plan and is four stories high.

facts.fact: In 1998–99 Martien van Goor renovated the building and an exhibition wing by Kisho Kurokawa was added.
facts.quote: In 1998 and 1999, the building was renovated by the Dutch architect Martien van Goor, and an exhibition wing by the Japanese architect Kisho Kurokawa was added.

facts.fact: The Kurokawa wing, used for major temporary exhibitions, has an oval plan and is reached by a tunnel from the Rietveld building.
facts.quote: It has an oval floor plan and is three stories high. The entrance to the Kurokawa wing is via a tunnel from the Rietveld building.

facts.fact: It opened in 1990 as part of Mito's centennial celebrations.
facts.quote: It opened in 1990 as part of the centennial celebrations of the municipality of Mito.

facts.fact: It holds a 680-seat concert hall, a theatre for up to 636, a contemporary art gallery and a 100-metre landmark tower.
facts.quote: There is a concert hall that seats 680, a theater for up to 636, a contemporary art gallery, and a landmark tower, which rises 100 meters.

facts.fact: Arata Isozaki was the architect, with acoustic design by Nagata Acoustics.
facts.quote: Arata Isozaki was the architect, with acoustical design by Nagata Acoustics.

facts.fact: The design is based on the Boerdijk–Coxeter helix.
facts.quote: The design is based on the Boerdijk–Coxeter helix.

facts.fact: It belongs to the more modernist style Isozaki developed later in his career.
facts.quote: Later he developed a more modernistic style with buildings such as the Art Tower of Mito (1986–90) and Domus-Casa del Hombre (1991–1995) in Galicia, Spain.

facts.fact: The concrete and metal church was built in 1965 in a long church style to plans by Jan Inge Hovig; it seats about 600.
facts.quote: The modern concrete and metal church was built in a long church style in 1965 using plans drawn up by architect Jan Inge Hovig. The church seats about 600 people.

facts.fact: Despite its nickname it is a parish church, not a cathedral.
facts.quote: Despite its nickname, it is a parish church and not, in fact, a cathedral as it is commonly called.

facts.fact: It is built of cast-in-place, aluminium-coated concrete panels.
facts.quote: The church is built out of cast-in-place aluminium-coated concrete panels.

facts.fact: Its shape is believed to refer to the nearby twin-peaked island of Håja.
facts.quote: The shape of the church is believed to be a reference to the nearby twin-peaked island of Håja.

facts.fact: In 1972 Victor Sparre's glass mosaic "The Return of Christ" was added on the east side.
facts.quote: In 1972, a glass mosaic titled "The Return of Christ" was added to the eastern side, made by Victor Sparre.

facts.fact: It is Hovig's most notable work, designed in 1960 and finished in 1965.
facts.quote: Hovig's most notable work is the Arctic Cathedral (Tromsdalen kirke), which was designed in 1960 and finished in 1965.

facts.fact: The Church of Saint Joan of Arc is a Catholic church in the centre of Rouen, France.
facts.quote: The Church of Saint Joan of Arc (French: L'église Sainte-Jeanne-d'Arc) is a Catholic church in the city centre of Rouen, northern France.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1979 in the old market square, the Place du Vieux-Marché, where Joan of Arc was burned at the stake in 1431.
facts.quote: The church of Saint Joan of Arc was completed in 1979 in the centre of the ancient market square, known as the Place du Vieux-Marché, the place where Joan of Arc was burned at the stake for heresy in 1431.

facts.fact: Louis Arretche, commissioned in 1969, designed the church and the market halls beside it.
facts.quote: The modern church Sainte-Jeanne d'Arc and the adjacent market halls were designed by the architect Louis Arretche, who was commissioned in 1969.

facts.fact: Its sweeping curves are meant to evoke both the flames that killed Joan of Arc and an overturned longship.
facts.quote: The sweeping curves of the structure are meant to evoke both the flames that consumed Joan of Arc and an overturned longship.

facts.fact: The tiled roof carries the same theme and forms a covered walkway over the square.
facts.quote: The tiled roof echoes this theme and forms a covered walkway over the square.

facts.fact: Its stained glass comes from the 16th-century Church of Saint Vincent, whose ruins stand a few metres away.
facts.quote: The stained glass windows come from the 16th century Church of Saint Vincent, whose ruins are located a few metres away.

facts.fact: The old church was almost destroyed in 1944, but its windows had been taken out and stored safely during the war.
facts.quote: The old church was almost completely destroyed in 1944 during World War II, but the windows had been removed and stored in a safe location during the war.

facts.fact: The Cidade das Artes is a cultural complex in Barra da Tijuca, Rio de Janeiro, first planned to open in 2004 as the Cidade da Música.
facts.quote: The Cidade das Artes (City of Arts) is a cultural complex located in Barra da Tijuca in the Southwest Zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, which was originally planned to open in 2004, with the name of Cidade da Música (City of Music).

facts.fact: It was formally opened in January 2013.
facts.quote: The formal inauguration was in January 2013, with the musical "Rock in Rio".

facts.fact: It is the home of the Brazilian Symphony Orchestra and the largest modern concert hall in South America, with 1,780 seats.
facts.quote: As the new home of the Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira (Brazilian Symphony Orchestra) and a main center for music, the Cidade das Artes is the largest modern concert hall in South America, with 1,780 seats.

facts.fact: The complex covers about 90,000 square metres and also has a chamber music hall, three theatres and 12 rehearsal rooms.
facts.quote: The complex spans approximately 90 thousand square metres and also features a chamber music hall, three theatres, and 12 rehearsal rooms.

facts.fact: Its terrace has panoramic views over Barra da Tijuca.
facts.quote: The terrace offers panoramic views of the neighbourhood of Barra da Tijuca.

facts.fact: It was designed by Christian de Portzamparc and paid for by the city of Rio de Janeiro.
facts.quote: The building was designed by the French architect Christian de Portzamparc and construction was funded by the city of Rio de Janeiro.

facts.fact: Its cost of R$515 million, against an original budget of R$86 million, caused much controversy.
facts.quote: The project's R$515 million (approx. US$250 million) to the city of Rio caused much controversy was originally budgeted at R$86 million.

facts.fact: Kerry and Lindsay Clare were Design Directors at Architectus for the Queensland Gallery of Modern Art, which won the National RAIA Award for Public Architecture in 2007.
facts.quote: The Clares were Design Directors for Architectus for notable projects including the Queensland Gallery of Modern Art (National RAIA Award for Public Architecture 2007), the University of the Sunshine Coast Chancellery (AIA State Public Architecture Award and the Harry S Marks Environment Award in 2008), the University of New South Wales student housing (2009), and the Brisbane Wesley House Commercial Building (2009).

facts.fact: The University City of Caracas, the campus the stadium belongs to, was designed by Carlos Raúl Villanueva and made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.
facts.quote: It was designed by the Venezuelan architect Carlos Raúl Villanueva and was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 2000.

facts.fact: After the designs changed in 1949, the campus stadiums were built in 1950 and opened in 1951.
facts.quote: In 1949 the initial designs were changed, with the stadiums being built in 1950 and inaugurated in 1951.

facts.fact: Building the stadiums began a new phase in developing the campus's Central Complex.
facts.quote: The stadiums construction signaled a new phase in developing the Conjunto Central (Central Complex) of the campus.

facts.fact: UNESCO singles out the Olympic Stadium among the campus's design elements.
facts.quote: The Olympic Stadium of the university is one of the design elements specifically highlighted by UNESCO.

facts.fact: It is mainly a football stadium, home of Caracas F.C., with seats for almost 24,000 people.
facts.quote: It is primarily an association football stadium, and the home ground of Caracas F.C.; it has seats for almost 24,000 people.

facts.fact: Besides the pitch it has a full-size running track and spaces for field events.
facts.quote: As well as the football pitch, the Olympic Stadium contains a full size running track and spaces for athletic field events, including jumping tracks and sandpits.

facts.fact: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni is an unfinished palace on the Grand Canal in Venice, near Santa Maria della Salute.
facts.quote: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni (Italian: Palazzo Venier dei Leoni) is an unfinished palace in Venice, Italy, located in the Dorsoduro district on the Grand Canal, near the Santa Maria della Salute basilica.

facts.fact: Lorenzo Boschetti designed it in 1749 for the Venier family.
facts.quote: The palazzo was designed in 1749 by architect Lorenzo Boschetti (author of the facade of the church San Barnaba) for the Venier family.

facts.fact: The design was meant to combine the styles of Palladio and Longhena.
facts.quote: The project envisioned a building that would combine the styles of Palladio and Longhena, two architects who left a significant legacy in Venice.

facts.fact: Because of the family's money problems, only part of the first floor was built.
facts.quote: However, the ambitious project remained unfinished: the Venier family's financial problems led to the construction of only part of the first floor of the palazzo.

facts.fact: A wooden model of the palazzo as planned can be seen in the Correr Museum.
facts.quote: In the Correr Museum, one can see a wooden model of what the completed palazzo would have looked like.

facts.fact: It is a single-storey, unfinished building with a rusticated façade of Istrian stone.
facts.quote: The building is a single-story, unfinished structure with a rusticated facade made of Istrian stone.

facts.fact: Peggy Guggenheim bought it in 1948 as her home and the venue for her modern art collection.
facts.quote: In 1948, Peggy Guggenheim purchased the palazzo, which became not only her Venetian home but also the venue for her small but valuable collection of modern art.

facts.fact: The Australian National Maritime Museum is a federal museum in Darling Harbour, Sydney.
facts.quote: The Australian National Maritime Museum (ANMM) is a federally operated maritime museum in Darling Harbour, Sydney.

facts.fact: It was built as part of Darling Harbour's redevelopment, a major draw meant to help the precinct succeed.
facts.quote: The building of the ANMM was seen by both the federal and New South Wales State governments as an important feature of the redevelopment, as it would be a major drawcard, and help fuel the commercial success of the precinct.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Philip Cox, Richardson Taylor & Partners.
facts.quote: The museum building was designed by Philip Cox, Richardson Taylor & Partners.

facts.fact: Its corrugated metal roof is shaped like billowing sails, over 25 metres tall on the west side and much lower on the east.
facts.quote: The roof was shaped to invoke the image of billowing sails: the corrugated metal roof stands over 25 metres (82 ft) tall on the west side, but drops significantly on the east.

facts.fact: Delays, cost overruns and funding disputes pushed the opening from 1988 to 1991.
facts.quote: The museum building was designed by Philip Cox, and although an opening date of 1988 was initially set, construction delays, cost overruns, and disagreements between the state and federal governments over funding responsibility pushed the opening to 1991.

facts.fact: Construction finished on 17 November 1989, at a cost that had risen to $70 million.
facts.quote: Construction was completed on 17 November 1989; the cost of the museum's construction had increased to $70 million, and although the federal government was willing to pay the initial $30 million, there were disagreements between the state and federal governments over who had to supply the additional $40 million.

facts.fact: Michael Rayner of Cox's firm was responsible for designing the museum.
facts.quote: Rayner was responsible for designing noted public buildings, including Australian National Maritime Museum and the Sydney Exhibition Centre (now demolished) in Darling Harbour.

facts.fact: The Dentsu Building is the headquarters tower of Dentsu in Shiodome, Minato, Tokyo.
facts.quote: The Dentsu Building or Dentsu Headquarters Building (電通本社ビル, Dentsū Honsha Biru) is a high-rise building in the Shiodome area of Minato, Tokyo, Japan.

facts.fact: It was designed by Jean Nouvel and completed in 2002.
facts.quote: It was designed by French architect Jean Nouvel and completed in 2002.

facts.fact: It has 48 floors and rises to 213.34 m.
facts.quote: 48 floors rise to 213.34 m (700 ft), it is the twelfth-tallest building in Tokyo and second-tallest in Shiodome, next to Shiodome City Center.

facts.fact: It stands on the site of Tokyo's first train station, beside the Hamarikyu Gardens.
facts.quote: It was built over the site of Tokyo's first train station, and sits aside the Hamarikyu Gardens, formerly the site of a shōgun's vacation home.

facts.fact: Roof collectors gather rainwater for its plumbing, and ceramic dots on the windows work with computer-controlled shades to cut climate-control costs.
facts.quote: The Dentsu building is an example of contemporary architecture, featuring collectors on the roof to utilize rainwater for its plumbing system, as well as ceramic dots on the windows which, in concert with computerized window shades, control climate control expenditure.

facts.fact: Except for sludge, all waste from its construction was recycled.
facts.quote: With the exception of sludge, all waste materials produced in the construction of the Dentsu Building were recycled.

facts.fact: Aurora Place in Sydney is two towers by Renzo Piano: an 18-storey residential building beside a 41-storey office tower, with metal and glass sunscreens on their roofs.
facts.quote: Aurora Place in Sydney, Australia (1996–2009) is composed of two towers, an eighteen-story residential building next to a forty-one story office building with different facades but similar metal and glass sunscreens on the roofs.

facts.fact: The office tower's east façade bulges out slightly from its base and is widest at the top floors.
facts.quote: The office tower has a discreetly peculiar form; the east façade bulges out slightly from its base, reaching its maximum width at the top floors.

facts.fact: The curved, twisted east façade echoes the Sydney Opera House on the harbour.
facts.quote: The curved and twisted shape of east the façade echoes that of the Sydney Opera House on the harbor.

facts.fact: The glass curtain wall extends beyond the main frame, so the wall seems independent of the building.
facts.quote: The exterior glass curtain-wall extends beyond the main frame, creating an illusion that the wall is independent of the building.

facts.fact: Piano designed an outer skin of glass and ceramics to control the strength of the sunlight.
facts.quote: Piano designed an exterior skin combining glass and ceramics to regulate the intensity of the sunlight.

facts.fact: The office building has indoor winter gardens on every floor, and earth-coloured ceramic tiles colour the façade.
facts.quote: The office building has interior winter gardens on each floor, and earth-colored ceramic tiles give a dash of color to the facade.

facts.fact: Saint-Nicolas is a Catholic church in Hérémence, Switzerland, known for its brutalist modern architecture.
facts.quote: Saint-Nicolas Church is a Catholic church in Hérémence, Switzerland, known for its brutalist modern architecture.

facts.fact: It was designed by Walter Maria Förderer.
facts.quote: It was designed by Walter Maria Förderer (March 21, 1928–June 29, 2006).

facts.fact: The theatre in Wolfsburg was one of Scharoun's important buildings finished only after his death in 1972.
facts.quote: Some of his most important buildings were only finished after his 1972 death in Berlin, including the German Maritime Museum in Bremerhaven, the theatre in Wolfsburg and the Berlin State Library.

facts.fact: The museum houses the Ara Pacis of Augustus, an ancient altar first inaugurated in 9 BC.
facts.quote: The Museum of the Ara Pacis (Italian: Museo dell'Ara Pacis) belongs to the Sistema dei Musei in Comune of Rome (Italy); it houses the Ara Pacis of Augustus, an ancient monument that was initially inaugurated on 30 January 9 B.C.

facts.fact: Designed by Richard Meier in steel, travertine, glass and plaster, it was the first major new building in Rome's historic centre since the Fascist era.
facts.quote: Designed by the American architect Richard Meier and built in steel, travertine, glass and plaster, the museum is the first major architectural and urban intervention in the historic centre of Rome since the Fascist era.

facts.fact: Wide glazing and skylights let light into the central pavilion.
facts.quote: Wide glazed surfaces and skylights allow the light to penetrate the central pavilion.

facts.fact: The travertine cladding replaced the aluminium first planned, after criticism of the building's impact on its surroundings.
facts.quote: The white color is a hallmark of Richard Meier's work, while the travertine plates decorating part of the building reflect design changes (aluminium surfaces were initially planned), resulting from a modification following criticism on the visual impact of the structure on the surrounding urban landscape.

facts.fact: It replaced a 1938 building by Vittorio Ballio Morpurgo, built as part of Mussolini's remaking of Piazza Augusto Imperatore.
facts.quote: The museum's first building was designed by architect Vittorio Ballio Morpurgo and completed in 1938, during the Fascist era, as part of Mussolini's reconfiguration of Piazza Augusto Imperatore.

facts.fact: Morpurgo's building was demolished, and Meier's opened on 21 April 2006 after seven years of work.
facts.quote: Morpurgo's building was demolished and the current building opened to the public, after seven years of works, on 21 April 2006 (the anniversary of the traditional date of the foundation of Rome).

facts.fact: The building has divided opinion: The New York Times judged it a flop.
facts.quote: The building has attracted conflicting opinions. The New York Times judged it a flop, "a contemporary expression of what can happen when an architect fetishizes his own style out of a sense of self-aggrandizement.

facts.fact: The Capitol Records Building is a 13-storey tower in Hollywood, Los Angeles.
facts.quote: The Capitol Records Building, also known as the Capitol Records Tower, is a 13-story tower building in the Hollywood neighborhood of Los Angeles, California, United States.

facts.fact: It was designed by Louis Naidorf of Welton Becket Associates and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: Designed by Louis Naidorf of Welton Becket Associates, it is one of the city's landmarks and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: It is considered the world's first circular office building.
facts.quote: The Capitol Records Building, designed by architect Louis Naidorf is considered to be the world's first circular office building ever constructed.

facts.fact: The design came from Naidorf's graduate school drawings; he was 24 when he designed it.
facts.quote: The building's design is based on the graduate school drawings of Louis Naidorf who, as the primary architect, designed the first circular office building when he was 24 years old.

facts.fact: Its wide curved awnings and tall spike look like a stack of records on a turntable, though this was a coincidence.
facts.quote: The wide curved awnings over windows on each story and the tall spike emerging from the top of the building resembles a stack of records on a turntable with the spindle pointing skyward. This resemblance, however, was coincidental, as Welton Becket kept the client's identity secret.

facts.fact: Capitol's president first wanted a rectangular building, but his lender felt the round design would attract attention.
facts.quote: Upon first seeing the design, Capitol Records' president Glen Wallichs insisted on a rectangular building, so Naidorf provided Wallichs with both. Wallichs presented both designs to his lender, who felt the round design would attract attention, which would make it easier to lease.

facts.fact: Its 13 storeys fit the 150-foot height limit then in force.
facts.quote: The 13-story building conforms to the 150-foot (46 m) zoning height limit in place at the time of its construction.

facts.fact: The light on top blinks "Hollywood" in Morse code.
facts.quote: The blinking light atop the tower spells out the word "Hollywood" in Morse code.

facts.fact: Casa Bloc is a housing building in Barcelona's Sant Andreu district, built between 1932 and 1936.
facts.quote: Casa Bloc is a residential building constructed between 1932 and 1936, located at 101 Passeig de Torras i Bages, in the Sant Andreu district of the city of Barcelona (Catalonia, Spain).

facts.fact: Sert, Subirana and Torres Clavé designed a large building of more than 200 flats for workers, many of whom then lived in shacks.
facts.quote: Josep Lluís Sert (1902-1983), Joan Baptista Subirana (1904-1978), and Josep Torres Clavé (1906-1939) designed a large building with more than 200 apartments for workers in the industrial district of Sant Andreu, many of whom at that time still lived in shacks, generally in very poor conditions.

facts.fact: It aimed to give decent low-cost housing while suggesting new forms of shared living and collective identity.
facts.quote: The GATCPAC members had sought to embody key elements of the group's thinking in the Casa Bloc, with a program designed to provide decent housing at low cost while suggesting new forms of social living and collective identity, formalized in a new urbanism based on a new concept of the city.

facts.fact: The Spanish Civil War stopped its completion.
facts.quote: The Spanish Civil War prevented the completion of the Casa Bloc and the conclusion of the three-year conflict put an end to the philosophy that had underpinned its construction.

facts.fact: In 1992 the Catalan government declared it a protected heritage monument.

facts.fact: Flat 1/11 is a 60 m² duplex.
facts.quote: The housing 1/11 is a duplex measuring 60 square meters.

facts.fact: Every room faces outside, and openings on both sides of the block give easy cross ventilation.

facts.fact: The Cathedral of Learning is a 42-storey skyscraper at the centre of the University of Pittsburgh's main campus.
facts.quote: The Cathedral of Learning is a 42-story skyscraper that serves as the centerpiece of the University of Pittsburgh's (Pitt) main campus in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

facts.fact: At 535 feet, the Late Gothic Revival tower is the tallest educational building in the Western Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Standing at 535 feet (163 m), the 42-story Late Gothic Revival structure is the tallest educational building in the Western Hemisphere and the second-tallest university building (fifth-tallest educationally purposed building) in the world, after the main building of Moscow State University.

facts.fact: Charles Klauder, a leading Gothic architect, was hired to design it; the design took two years and tried to fuse a modern skyscraper with Gothic ideals.
facts.quote: One of the foremost Gothic architects of the time, Philadelphian Charles Klauder, was hired to design the tower. The design took two years to finish, with the final plan attempting to fuse the idea of a modern skyscraper with the tradition and ideals of Gothic architecture.

facts.fact: It is a steel frame clad in Indiana limestone, with more than 2,000 rooms and windows.
facts.quote: Colloquially referred to as "Cathy" by Pitt students, the Cathedral of Learning is a steel-frame structure overlaid with Indiana limestone and contains more than 2,000 rooms and windows.

facts.fact: Commissioned in 1921, it was begun in 1926, first used for classes in 1931 and formally dedicated in June 1937.
facts.quote: The Cathedral of Learning was commissioned in 1921 and ground was broken in 1926 under general contractor Stone & Webster. The first class was held in the building in 1931 and its exterior finished in October 1934, prior to its formal dedication in June 1937.

facts.fact: The Commons Room is a four-storey, half-acre hall in 15th-century English Perpendicular Gothic style.
facts.quote: The main part of the cathedral's first floor, the Commons Room, called one of the "great architectural fantasies of the twentieth century", is a fifteenth-century English perpendicular Gothic-style hall that covers half an acre (2,000 m2) and extends upward four stories, reaching 52 feet (16 m) tall.

facts.fact: Guastavino acoustic tiles between the vault ribs keep the Commons Room quiet.
facts.quote: Despite its heavy use, the Commons Room is kept quiet by the use of Guastavino acoustical tiles as the stones between the ribs of vaulting.

facts.fact: It holds 31 Nationality Rooms, classrooms designed by Pittsburgh's ethnic communities in the styles of different nations.
facts.quote: The lobby, comprising the first through third floors, contains a massive gothic Commons Room that is used as a general study area and for special events and is ringed by three floors of classrooms, including, on the first and third floors, the 31 Nationality Rooms designed by members of Pittsburgh's ethnic communities in the styles of different nations and ethnic groups.

facts.fact: The Cuvilliés Theatre is the former court theatre of the Residenz in Munich.
facts.quote: The Cuvilliés Theatre (German: Cuvilliés-Theater) or Old Residence Theatre (Altes Residenztheater) is the former court theatre of the Residenz in Munich, Bavaria, Germany.

facts.fact: François de Cuvilliés built it in the Rococo style between 1751 and 1753, with carving supervised by Johann Baptist Straub.
facts.quote: The Residence Theatre was built from 1751 to 1753 by François de Cuvilliés in rococo style. The carving was done under supervision of Johann Baptist Straub.

facts.fact: The carved, gilded boxes survived wartime bombing because they had been taken down and stored beforehand.
facts.quote: Though the theatre was bombed during World War II, the carved and gilded boxes could be reused for they had been dismantled before and stored for security.

facts.fact: The theatre was carefully recreated in the 1950s and reopened in 1958.
facts.quote: Afterwards the Residenztheater was meticulously recreated in the 1950s and re-opened in 1958 under the name Cuvilliés Theatre with a performance of Mozart's The Marriage of Figaro.

facts.fact: The hall is red and gold, with four tiers of 14 boxes forming a horseshoe around the ground floor.
facts.quote: The theatre space is decorated in red and gold. The four floors, each with 14 loges enclose the ground floor in the shape of a horseshoe.

facts.fact: The Electoral box facing the stage spans two tiers and is held up by two Atlas figures.
facts.quote: Particularly noteworthy is the Electoral loge opposite the stage that extends from the second to third tier. It is supported by two figures of Atlas, which form the entrance.

facts.fact: Mozart's Idomeneo had its premiere there in 1781.
facts.quote: Many operas were staged there by the Bavarian court opera, including the premieres of Mozart's Idomeneo in 1781 and Weber's Abu Hassan in 1811.

facts.fact: It was renovated and modernised from 2004 to 2008.
facts.quote: The theatre was again renovated and technically modernised from 2004 to 2008.

facts.fact: The hospital is owned and run by Emergency, an international NGO.
facts.quote: It is a hospital, owned and operated by Emergency, an international NGO that offers "free medical treatment to the victims of war, poverty and landmines".

facts.fact: It offers free children's surgery to patients from Uganda and across Africa.
facts.quote: It also offers free pediatric surgical care to Children from Uganda and across Africa.

facts.fact: It sits on 30 acres of land.

facts.fact: It was designed by Renzo Piano and built with TAM Associates.
facts.quote: The hospital was designed by Renzo Piano and built in association with TAM Associates.

facts.fact: It opened on 19 April 2021 with 72 beds.
facts.quote: Opened on 19 April 2021, the hospital has bed capacity of 72 patients.

facts.fact: Construction was reported to cost about €29 million.
facts.quote: The Kampala Post, a Ugandan online publication, reported the construction cost to be USh117 billion in 2021 (approx. €29 million).

facts.fact: The McGregor Memorial Conference Center is a meeting building at Wayne State University in Detroit, designed by Minoru Yamasaki and completed in 1958.
facts.quote: The McGregor Memorial Conference Center is a meeting and event facility on the campus of Wayne State University in Midtown Detroit, Michigan, designed by noted American architect Minoru Yamasaki (1912–1986) and completed in 1958.

facts.fact: It marks Yamasaki's shift from the International Style to New Formalism.
facts.quote: The design marks a shift in style from Yamasaki's earlier International Style work to the New Formalism of his later years.

facts.fact: It is a two-storey, symmetrical pavilion clad in travertine marble.
facts.quote: The McGregor Memorial Conference Center is a two-story symmetrical pavilion covered with travertine marble.

facts.fact: It sits on a podium of Mankato stone, with a reflecting pool and sunken garden wrapping two sides.
facts.quote: It sits on a podium faced with Mankato stone, with integral reflecting pool and sunken garden wrapping around the building on two sides.

facts.fact: A triangular motif runs outside and in; a skylit entry hall divides the interior, flanked by two levels of conference rooms.
facts.quote: The building exhibits a triangular design motif on the outside and inside. Inside, a skylit entry hall, dividing the interior space in two, is flanked by two levels of conference rooms.

facts.fact: The American Institute of Architects gave Yamasaki a First Honor Award for it.
facts.quote: The center was completed in 1958, and opened to immediate accolades from architectural magazines who called it "delightful" and "refreshing," and from the American Institute of Architects who awarded Yamasaki a First Honor Award for the design.

facts.fact: It became a National Historic Landmark in 2015 for its architecture.
facts.quote: The building was designated a National Historic Landmark for its architectural quality in 2015.

facts.quote: SOM also provided the schematic design of structure and MEP and the detailed structural design of the roof.

facts.fact: The X-shaped terminal has 450,000 m² of floor space on four floors, for both domestic and international passengers.
facts.quote: The X-shaped terminal has a total floor area of 450,000 square metres (4,800,000 sq ft) across four floors and handles both domestic and international passengers.

facts.fact: Gates sit on two piers running south from a central building whose 42-metre-high roof uses over 20,000 tonnes of steel and covers 30 acres.
facts.quote: The structure has boarding gates on two piers extending southwards from a central processing building featuring a 42-metre (138 ft) high roof employing over 20,000 metric tonnes of fabricated steel covering 30 acres (12 ha).

facts.fact: The project was estimated to cost about US$1 billion and employ over 12,000 workers.
facts.quote: The entire project was estimated to cost ₹98 billion (US$1.0 billion) and employ over 12,000 workers.

facts.fact: The old terminal 2A was demolished in 2009 and the new terminal opened five years later, in January 2014.

facts.fact: The mosque stands in the centre of Dhaka and was completed in 1968.

facts.quote: The mosque has several modern architectural features whilst preserving the traditional principles of Mughal architecture which has for some time been dominant in the Indian sub-continent.

facts.fact: It has no dome; two domed entrance porches, south and north, make up for it.
facts.quote: The absence of a dome on the main building is compensated by the two superficial domed entrance porticoes, one on the south, and the other on the north.

facts.fact: Two open courtyards bring light and air into the prayer hall.
facts.quote: Two patios (roofless inner courtyard) ensure that enough light and air enter the prayer hall of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque.

facts.fact: On completion in 2010 it became the tallest building in Vietnam, until January 2011.
facts.quote: At its completion in 2010, it became the tallest building in Vietnam and kept this status until January 2011, when it was surpassed by Keangnam Hanoi Landmark Tower.

facts.fact: It has 68 floors above ground and stands 262.5 metres tall.
facts.quote: With 68 floors above ground and three basements, the building has a height of 262.5 metres (861 ft), making it the second tallest building in the city, fourth tallest in Vietnam, and the 412th tallest in the world, as of May 2022.

facts.fact: It was designed by Carlos Zapata, with AREP as architect of record.
facts.quote: The tower was designed by Carlos Zapata, Design Principal and Founder of Carlos Zapata Studio, with AREP as architect of record.

facts.fact: Its shape was inspired by the lotus, Vietnam's national flower.
facts.quote: Designed by Carlos Zapata, drew inspiration for this skyscraper's unique shape from Vietnam's national flower, the Lotus.

facts.fact: Each of its 6,000 glass panels is cut differently because every floor is unique.
facts.quote: Each of the 6,000 sleek glass panels enveloping the Bitexco Financial Tower is individually cut to unique specifications because each floor is unique, giving the building its eye-catching shape.

facts.fact: Vietnam's first non-rooftop helipad sticks out 22 metres from the 52nd floor.
facts.quote: Vietnam's first non-rooftop helipad is on the 52nd floor of the tower, it extends 22 meters out from the main structure and strong enough to carry a helicopter up to 3 tons of weight.

facts.fact: In 2013 CNN named it one of 25 Great Skyscraper Icons of Construction.
facts.quote: In 2013, CNN named the Bitexco Financial Tower one of the 25 Great Skyscraper Icons of Construction.

facts.fact: Centenary Park is an 11-acre (4.5 ha) park on the Chulalongkorn University campus in Bangkok.
facts.quote: Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park (Thai: อุทยาน 100 ปี จุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย) is a 28-rai (4.5 ha; 11-acre) park located on the campus of Chulalongkorn University in Bangkok, Thailand.

facts.fact: It was completed in 2017 for the university's 100th anniversary.
facts.quote: It was completed in 2017 to honor the 100th anniversary of the university's founding.

facts.fact: Landscape architects Landprocess designed it as a rainwater detention basin, partly inspired by King Bhumibol's 'monkey cheeks' project.
facts.quote: Designed by landscape architecture firm Landprocess, Centenary Park was designed to serve as a rainwater detention basin, partially inspired by the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej's monkey cheeks project.

facts.fact: It was the first central plot in 30 years of Bangkok's rapid growth set aside as public green space instead of commercial development.
facts.quote: It was the first time in 30 years of rapid urban development that a centrally located 11-acre plot of land, including a 1.3-kilometer stretch of road and valued at an estimated US$700 million, was designated as public green space rather than for commercial development.

facts.fact: The park sits on a three-degree slope, with artificial wetlands and underground tanks holding one million gallons of water.
facts.quote: The park is built on a three degree incline and contains artificial wetlands and underground cisterns that can hold one million gallons (3.8 million litres) of water.

facts.fact: Its ecological parts show a way of living with water rather than fearing it.
facts.quote: It was designed with various ecological components that reflect an approach to adapting to and managing the city's relationship with water, rather than fearing it.

facts.fact: The station, in the historic Ulus quarter, is a landmark of Ankara.
facts.quote: Located within the historic Ulus quarter, the station is a landmark of the city.

facts.quote: The current Art deco building was built in 1937 by Turkish architect Şekip Akalın.

facts.quote: When President Mustafa Kemal Atatürk requested that a Turkish architect be selected for the design of the new Ankara railway station building in 1935, Akalın was chosen as the project's architect at age 25.

facts.fact: Akalın travelled in Europe and took the Art Deco style sweeping the continent for the station.
facts.quote: He then traveled to Europe to prepare a design for the station. He was inspired by the wave of Art deco architecture sweeping the continent as he went on to design Ankara station's building in that style.

facts.fact: The station was completed in 1937, when Akalın was 27.
facts.quote: The station was completed in 1937, when Akalın was 27 years old.

facts.fact: Turkey's Chamber of Civil Engineers lists it among the country's fifty civil engineering feats.
facts.quote: The Turkish Chamber of Civil Engineers lists Ankara Central Station as one of the fifty civil engineering feats in Turkey, a list of remarkable engineering projects realized in the first 50 years of the chamber.

facts.fact: The Aérohabitat is a housing complex in Algiers, built between 1952 and 1955.
facts.quote: The Aérohabitat is a residence located in Algiers, built between 1952 and 1955 by Louis Miquel and José Ferrer-Laloë.

facts.fact: Built as a raised horizontal block, it set out to make a new kind of city, a "vertical village".
facts.quote: Constructed as a raised horizontal block, it aimed to materialize a new form of city, a "vertical village" called Unité d'habitation (Housing Unit).

facts.fact: It is credited to Louis Miquel with Pierre Bourlier and José Ferrer-Laloë, all members of CIAM-Algiers.
facts.quote: The construction of the Aérohabitat is attributed to Louis Miquel, along with Pierre Bourlier and José Ferrer-Laloë, all members of CIAM-Algiers (International Congresses of Modern Architecture).

facts.fact: It has four buildings and 300 apartments.
facts.quote: It consists of four buildings and 300 apartments.

facts.fact: It follows Le Corbusier's idea of "immeuble-villas".
facts.quote: The Aérohabitat falls within the concept of "immeuble-villas" initiated by the Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier.

facts.fact: Miquel put an interior street, like a shopping gallery, at mid-height of the main building.
facts.quote: Miquel incorporated the principle of an interior street at mid-height of the main building, resembling a commercial gallery.

facts.fact: Unlike Le Corbusier's internal corridors, the flats are reached by outside circulation.
facts.quote: In contrast to Le Corbusier's concept of internal circulation, Miquel opted for an exterior circulation system that serves the apartments.

facts.fact: The Bavinger House in Norman, Oklahoma, was designed by Bruce Goff and completed in 1955.
facts.quote: The Bavinger House was completed in 1955 in Norman, Oklahoma, United States. It was designed by architect Bruce Goff.

facts.fact: Seen as a key example of organic architecture, it won the AIA's Twenty-five Year Award in 1987.
facts.quote: Considered a significant example of organic architecture, the house was awarded the Twenty-five Year Award from the American Institute of Architects in 1987.

facts.fact: The owners, artists Nancy and Eugene Bavinger, built it themselves over five years with students and volunteers.
facts.quote: The house was constructed over the course of five years by Nancy and Eugene Bavinger, the residents of the house, who were artists, along with the help of a few of Eugene's art students, volunteers, and local businesses.

facts.fact: Its wall was a 96-foot logarithmic spiral of 200 tons of local sandstone.
facts.quote: The wall of the house was a 96-foot long logarithmically curved spiral, made from 200 tons of local "ironrock" sandstone dynamited (by Eugene) from a piece of purchased farmland near Robin Hill School, a few miles away from the house and hauled back on Eugene's 1948 Chevy flatbed truck.

facts.fact: A reused oil-field drill stem formed a central mast over 55 feet high that anchored the structure.
facts.quote: The structure was anchored by a recycled oil field drill stem that was reused to make a central mast more than 55 feet high.

facts.fact: There were no interior walls, only platforms at different heights, some with curtains for privacy.
facts.quote: The house had no interior walls; instead there were a series of platforms at different heights, some with curtains that could be drawn for privacy.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2001 and removed in 2017, the year after it was demolished.
facts.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2001, and was removed from the National Register in 2017 after being demolished the previous year.

facts.fact: The 4x4 House is a private house by Tadao Ando in Tarumi-ku, Kobe, on the coast of the Inland Sea.
facts.quote: The 4x4 house is a private residential house designed by the Japanese architect Tadao Ando and located in Tarumi-ku, Kobe, Hyogo, on the coast of the Inland Sea in Japan.

facts.fact: It was built in 2003, on a lot of about 65 m².

facts.fact: It is a four-storey tower, 4 m by 4 m in plan.

facts.fact: Bedrooms are on the middle floors, with the kitchen and living room on top.

facts.fact: The top floor is a 4 m cube shifted exactly 1 m toward the sea, giving a feeling of being at sea.
facts.quote: The last floor is a 4x4m cube that is displaced exactly 1m from the vertical axis of the building in the direction of the water, giving a sensation of being at sea when looking at the horizon.

facts.fact: It is set deep in the ground and encased in concrete to resist lateral forces.
facts.quote: The house is encased in concrete and deep in the ground to resist to lateral forces.

facts.fact: MALBA, the Latin American Art Museum of Buenos Aires, stands on Figueroa Alcorta Avenue in Palermo.

facts.quote: This building was one of the first high-rise buildings to be constructed in Europe: it was the third-tallest pre-war skyscraper after Madrid's Telefónica Building and Antwerp's Boerentoren.

facts.fact: Designed by Vladimír Karfík in a Constructivist style, it was built from 1936 to 1938.
facts.quote: The building is in the style of Constructivist architecture, designed by Vladimír Karfík. It was built between 1936 and 1938 at the direction of company president Jan Antonín Baťa, who took over following the death of his half-brother Tomáš Baťa.

facts.fact: Its frame is reinforced concrete with spirally reinforced round columns.
facts.quote: The support system is formed by a reinforced concrete skeleton with characteristic cylindrical columns, which are spirally reinforced.

facts.fact: The director's office was a 6 × 6 m air-conditioned lift.
facts.quote: A technical rarity is the air conditioned lift office of the company director measuring 6 × 6 meters.

facts.fact: Each floor had its own heating and air-conditioning controls.
facts.quote: Each floor had its own heating and air conditioning controls independent of the rest of the building.

facts.fact: It was made a cultural monument of the Czech Republic in 1958.
facts.quote: In 1958 the building earned the cultural monument of the Czech Republic status (it is listed under number 1894).

facts.fact: Estadio Azteca is a football stadium in Coyoacán, Mexico City.
facts.quote: Estadio Azteca (Latin American Spanish: [esˈtaðjo asˈteka]), officially known as Estadio Banorte for sponsorship reasons, is a football stadium located in Coyoacán, Mexico City.

facts.fact: Designed by Pedro Ramírez Vázquez and Rafael Mijares Alcérreca, it broke ground in 1961 and opened on 29 May 1966 for 107,494 spectators.
facts.quote: Designed by architects Pedro Ramírez Vázquez and Rafael Mijares Alcérreca, the stadium broke ground in 1961 and the inaugural match was between Club América and Torino F.C. on 29 May 1966, with a capacity for 107,494 spectators.

facts.fact: With 87,523 seats it is the largest stadium in Latin America.
facts.quote: With a capacity of 87,523, it is the largest stadium in Latin America and the eighth-largest association football stadium in the world.

facts.fact: It was the first stadium to host two World Cup finals, in 1970 and 1986.
facts.quote: One of the best known football stadiums in the world, often called the "Temple of Football" or the "Cathedral of Football", it was the first to host two FIFA World Cup finals; Brazil defeated Italy 4–1 in 1970 and Argentina beat West Germany 3–2 in 1986.

facts.fact: It was the main football venue of the 1968 Summer Olympics.
facts.quote: The stadium was the principal venue for the football tournament of the 1968 Summer Olympics and the 1971 Women's World Cup.

facts.fact: It hosted the 2026 World Cup's opening game, making it the only stadium to host three World Cups.
facts.quote: It also hosted games during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including the opening game where South Africa played against Mexico, making it the only stadium to host three editions of the FIFA World Cup.

facts.fact: A renovation raised capacity from 83,000 to 87,500, added new video screens and laid a hybrid turf pitch.
facts.quote: The seating capacity was increased from 83,000 to 87,500 spectators, new video screens were installed, and a hybrid turf pitch was laid.

facts.fact: Most SNP, the 'UFO Bridge', is a road bridge over the Danube in Bratislava.
facts.quote: Most SNP ("Bridge of the Slovak National Uprising"), commonly referred to as Most Slovenského národného povstania or the UFO Bridge, and named Nový most ("New Bridge") from 1993 to 2012, is a road bridge over the Danube in Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia.

facts.fact: It is the world's longest bridge with one pylon and one cable-stayed plane.
facts.quote: It is the world's longest bridge to have one pylon and one cable-stayed plane.

facts.fact: It is an asymmetrical cable-stayed bridge with a 303 m main span and a total length of 430.8 m.
facts.quote: Most SNP is an asymmetrical cable-stayed bridge with a main span length of 303 m (994 ft), a total length of 430.8 m (1,413 ft), a width of 21 m (69 ft), and a weight of 537 t (592 short tons).

facts.fact: Cars use four lanes on the upper level; cyclists and pedestrians the lower level.
facts.quote: There are four lanes for motor traffic on the upper level and lanes for bicycles and pedestrians on the lower level.

facts.fact: Built from 1967 to 1972 under A. Tesár, J. Lacko and I. Slameň, it opened on 26 August 1972.
facts.quote: The bridge was built between 1967 and 1972 under a project managed by A. Tesár, J. Lacko and I. Slameň. It officially opened on August 26, 1972.

facts.fact: Much of the Old Town below, including nearly all the Jewish quarter, was demolished for its approach road.
facts.quote: A significant section of the Old Town below which included nearly all of the Jewish quarter, was demolished to create the roadway that led to it.

facts.fact: A saucer-shaped structure on the 84.6 m pylon holds an observation deck and restaurant.
facts.quote: A special attraction is the flying saucer-shaped structure atop the bridge's 84.6 m (278 ft) pylon, housing an observation deck and a restaurant, which since 2005 has been called UFO (previously, Bystrica).

facts.fact: Onagawa Station is a terminus of the Ishinomaki Line.
facts.quote: Onagawa Station is a terminal station on the Ishinomaki Line, located 44.9 kilometers from the opposing terminus of the line at Kogota Station.

facts.fact: The tsunami of 11 March 2011 destroyed the station building and nearby tracks.
facts.quote: Operations were suspended after the tsunami on March 11, 2011 which destroyed the station building and nearby railway tracks.

facts.fact: The rebuilt station reopened on 21 March 2015, completing the line's restoration.
facts.quote: Just over four years later, on March 21, 2015, the reconstructed Onagawa Station reopened marking the restoration of the entire Ishinomaki Line.

facts.fact: The new building holds a community centre and public bath on its upper floors.
facts.quote: The new station building features an integrated community center and public bathing facility on the upper floors.

facts.fact: It was designed by Shigeru Ban, who also helped design the town's temporary housing after the tsunami.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Pritzker Architecture Prize winning architect Shigeru Ban, who also contributed to the design of temporary housing structures in the town in the wake of the March 2011 tsunami.

facts.fact: In 1958, while the church was being built, Seinäjoki held a competition for a new town hall on a site next to the church.
facts.quote: In 1958, as the church was being built, the town of Seinäjoki organized another architectural competition for the design of a new town hall for a site next to the church.

facts.fact: Alvar and Elissa Aalto won that competition in 1959; it also covered a library, a theatre and a state office building, and the town hall was built in 1961–1962.
facts.quote: Alvar Aalto and his wife, Elissa Aalto, won the follow-up competition in 1959, which also included plans for a library, a theatre, and a state office building. The town hall was constructed in 1961–1962 and the library in 1964–1965.

facts.fact: The town hall is one of six buildings in the Aalto Centre, Seinäjoki's administrative and cultural centre, mainly completed between 1960 and 1968.
facts.quote: Aalto Center (Finnish: Aaltokeskus) is the administrative and cultural center of the City of Seinäjoki, Finland. It comprises six buildings, designed by Alvar Aalto and mainly completed between 1960 and 1968.

facts.fact: The centre is counted among Aalto's most important works and is known internationally as an architectural whole.
facts.quote: The center represents one of Aalto's most important works and is notable in Finland and even internationally as an architectural whole.

facts.fact: Aalto also designed the courtyard between the buildings, with a fountain and outdoor lighting.
facts.quote: Aalto also designed the courtyard between the buildings, including a fountain and the outdoor lighting.

facts.fact: The wooden plan of the centre is in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
facts.quote: The wooden plan of the center is in the collections of the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

facts.fact: In July 2026 the Aalto Centre was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with 12 other Aalto works.
facts.quote: In July 2026, the Aalto Center, along with 12 other Aalto Works, was designated by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: Tautra Abbey (Tautra Mariakloster) on the island of Tautra is a convent of Trappist nuns.
facts.quote: Tautra Abbey (Tautra Mariakloster), Tautra: Trappist nuns

facts.fact: The station opened in 1959 and was then the largest train station in China.
facts.quote: The Beijing railway station opened in 1959 and was the largest train station in China at the time.

facts.fact: With gilded eaves and tall clock towers, its architecture blends traditional Chinese and socialist realist influences.
facts.quote: With gilded eaves and soaring clock towers, the architecture of the railway blends traditional Chinese and socialist realist influence.

facts.fact: It was one of the 'Ten Great Buildings' planned in 1958 for the tenth anniversary of the People's Republic of China.
facts.quote: To commemorate the Tenth Anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party in 1958 began the planning and construction of ten large-scale projects, known as the "Ten Great Buildings" to showcase the new outlook of the country and the Beijing railway station was amongst the projects undertaken.

facts.fact: Premier Zhou Enlai proposed the turrets on each of the two wings of the main building, and the idea was adopted.
facts.quote: In determining the design program proposal, Zhou Enlai proposed that turrets be built on each of the two wings of the main building and this suggestion was adopted.

facts.fact: Construction began on 20 January 1959 and the station was finished on 10 September 1959, in just over seven months.
facts.quote: In just over seven months, the project was completed on 10 September 1959.

facts.fact: It was China's first large modern railway terminal.
facts.quote: The Beijing railway station was one of the largest construction projects in mainland China during that time with modern facilities and it was also China's first large modern railway terminal.

facts.fact: The south-facing station house mixed a traditional Chinese style with Soviet Stalinist architecture.
facts.quote: The Station house building faced south and the architecture included both a Chinese traditional style and the Soviet Stalinist architecture.

facts.fact: Its twelve waiting rooms, 14,000 square metres in all, could hold 14,000 passengers.
facts.quote: The twelve passenger waiting rooms comprised a total area of fourteen thousand square meters and was able to accommodate 14,000 waiting passengers.

facts.fact: The Coliseu do Porto is a theatre and concert venue in Porto that holds 4,000 standing.
facts.quote: The Coliseum of Porto (Portuguese: Coliseu do Porto) is a Portuguese theatre and concert venue in the municipality of Porto, in northern Portugal, with a capacity for a standing audience of 4000.

facts.fact: It is an example of Portuguese Streamline Moderne and Art Deco in Porto.
facts.quote: A leading venue for music and cultural events in Porto, together with Batalha Cinema, the Coliseu is an example of Portuguese Streamline Moderne and Art Deco styles in the city of Porto.

facts.fact: Cassiano Branco became principal architect of the new building in 1939, assisted by Júlio de Brito.
facts.quote: The following year, Cassiano Branco assumed the position of principal architect for the new project, with the assistance of Júlio de Brito.

facts.fact: Charles Ciclis, who had designed Paris theatres, was invited to work on it, but only his chandeliers and doors seem to have been used.
facts.quote: Charles Ciclis, who authored various projects in Parisian theatres, was also invited by Cassiano Branco to work on the Coliseum project. Of his interior designs, apparently only the candelabras and doors were included in the final design, although Ciclis was never remunerated.

facts.fact: The building opened on 19 December 1941.
facts.quote: The completed building opened on 19 December 1941.

facts.fact: A public campaign stopped its sale to a church in 1995, and the city council bought it in 1996.
facts.quote: This move resulted in the establishment of the Associação "Amigos do Coliseu do Porto", who helped stop its sale and protect the building. On 28 September 1996, a public deed for the purchase of the coliseum by the municipal council, which included the cinema Passos Manuel, the Garden-hall, attic hall and a lithography for 680,000 contos.

facts.fact: Between 1997 and 2001 the auditorium was completely rebuilt to improve acoustics and sightlines.
facts.quote: The auditorium was completely rebuilt to improve the acoustics and the visibility of the spectators, while a warehouse was built under the auditorium.

facts.fact: It was classified as a Property of Public Interest.
facts.quote: The Secretary of State for Culture ratified its classification as a Property of Public Interest.

facts.fact: AAMI Park, officially Melbourne Rectangular Stadium, is used mainly for soccer and rugby league.
facts.quote: Melbourne Rectangular Stadium (known under naming rights as AAMI Park) is a stadium located in the Melbourne Sports and Entertainment Precinct in Melbourne. It is primarily used for soccer, and rugby league as the home ground of the Melbourne Victory FC and Melbourne City FC in the A-League men's and women's competitions and the Melbourne Storm in the National Rugby League (NRL).

facts.fact: Built in 2010, it was Melbourne's first large stadium purpose-built for rectangular-field sports.
facts.quote: Built in 2010, the stadium replaced Olympic Park as Melbourne’s primary rectangular stadium, with it also being the first large stadium to be purpose built for rectangular sports, as Olympic Park was designed for Track and Field.

facts.fact: It seats 30,050, making it Melbourne's third largest stadium.
facts.quote: Boasting a capacity of 30,050, it is Melbourne’s third largest stadium.

facts.fact: COX Architecture's 'Bioframe' design uses a geodesic dome roof over most of the seats that still lets light reach the pitch.
facts.quote: The COX Architecture designed stadium features a "Bioframe" design, with a geodesic dome roof covering much of the seating area, while still allowing light through to the pitch.

facts.fact: The outside is covered in thousands of programmable LED lights that can show patterns and images.
facts.quote: The exterior of the stadium is covered in thousands of LED lights which can be programmed to display a variety of patterns and images.

facts.fact: Its foundations allow expansion to 50,000, but the roof was not designed for it, so expansion would need major work.
facts.quote: Although the stadium was built with foundations to allow for future expansion to 50,000, the roof was not designed with this in mind, and so the stadium cannot be expanded without major construction work.

facts.fact: During construction it was nicknamed the Bubble Dome.
facts.quote: The stadium was referred to as Melbourne Rectangular Stadium, Swan Street Stadium or the Bubble Dome during its early construction.

facts.fact: The Christchurch Art Gallery (Te Puna o Waiwhetū) is the public art gallery of Christchurch, New Zealand.
facts.quote: The Christchurch Art Gallery (Māori: Te Puna o Waiwhetū) is the public art gallery of the city of Christchurch, New Zealand.

facts.fact: It opened on 10 May 2003, replacing the Robert McDougall Art Gallery of 1932.
facts.quote: The gallery opened on 10 May 2003, replacing the city's previous public art gallery, the Robert McDougall Art Gallery, which had opened in 1932.

facts.fact: A design competition for the new gallery was launched in 1998.
facts.quote: A competition to design the new gallery was launched in 1998.

facts.fact: The building was designed by the Buchan Group.
facts.quote: The gallery's building was designed by the Buchan Group.

facts.fact: It was designed for earthquakes: its foundation is a concrete raft slab sitting on the ground surface that spreads earthquake forces evenly.
facts.quote: The gallery was designed to deal with seismic events. The gallery's foundation, a concrete raft slab that sits on the surface of the ground, evenly distributes earthquake forces.

facts.fact: After the 2011 earthquake it served as Civil Defence headquarters for seven months and reopened only on 19 December 2015.
facts.quote: The gallery building was used as a Civil Defence headquarters for seven months after the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, and did not reopen until 19 December 2015 due to the need for extensive refurbishments and improvements.

facts.fact: La Grande Borne is a housing estate on the southern outskirts of Paris, in Grigny and Viry-Châtillon.
facts.quote: La Grande Borne is a housing estate, in the Essonne département on the southern outskirts of Paris, France. The estate is located in both the communes of Grigny and Viry-Châtillon.

facts.fact: It was designed by the architect Émile Aillaud.
facts.quote: The architect Émile Aillaud designed this housing estate.

facts.fact: Aillaud's estates such as La Grande Borne (1964–1971) tried to offset the sameness of prefabricated concrete-panel building with more individual planning.
facts.quote: His designs can be found after World War II in France, such as Les Courtilières in Pantin (1955–1956, 1957–1960), Wiesberg at Forbach (1959, 1961 ff.) and La Grande Borne at Grigny (1964–1971), are representative of the attempts to compensate for the uniformity which resulted from extensively industrialized constructional methods (principally heavy construction employing prefabricated reinforced-concrete panels) by adopting more individualizing urban planning strategies.

facts.fact: This is done through smooth, abstract building masses in curving serpentine layouts, works of art, and colourful, oddly shaped public spaces.
facts.quote: This is chiefly achieved in the overall arrangement of the building masses, reduced to smooth abstract forms, in curved serpentine compositions; through the integration of works of art; and finally through the careful handling of public spaces, at times eccentrically shaped and colourfully treated.

facts.fact: The aim is to help residents identify with their surroundings.
facts.quote: The residents are thereby given an impetus to identify with their environment.

facts.fact: The Grande halle de la Villette, once the Great Hall of Cattle, was a slaughterhouse market and is now a cultural centre in Paris.
facts.quote: The Grande halle de la Villette (originally: Grande Halle aux Boeufs; translation: "Great Hall of Cattle"), formerly a slaughterhouse and now a cultural center, is located in Paris, France.

facts.fact: Designed by Jules de Mérindol and Louis-Adolphe Janvier, it was built in 1865–1867, and it is the only one of the complex's three market halls to survive.
facts.quote: Designed by Jules de Mérindol and Louis-Adolphe Janvier (1818–1878), construction of the Grande Halle took place during the period of 1865–1867. While the La Villette complex opened in the 1860s with a total of three market halls, only the Grande Halle aux Boeufs, preserved for its architectural value, survives.

facts.fact: Haussmann proposed gathering all of Paris's abattoirs and meat markets at La Villette on the city's edge.
facts.quote: As part of Haussmann's renovation of Paris, Baron Georges-Eugène Haussmann proposed concentrating all the abattoirs and meat markets on the city's outskirts at La Villette.

facts.fact: Bernard Reichen and Philippe Robert were chosen in 1982 to restore it, and Mitterrand opened the restored hall in January 1985.
facts.quote: François Mitterrand's 1982 announcement of Les Grands Projets' included Parc de la Villette, and in that year, Bernard Reichen and Philippe Robert were selected for the Grande Halle's restoration. After renovation completion, Mitterrand opened the restored Grande Halle in January 1985.

facts.fact: The hall is made of cast iron and glass and measures 250 by 85 metres, covering 20,000 square metres.
facts.quote: The Grande Halle is made of cast iron and glass. It covers an area of 20,000 square metres (220,000 sq ft), and measures 250 metres (820 ft) by 85 metres (279 ft).

facts.fact: Three sides are open and the fourth, of glass, is the entrance.
facts.quote: Three sides are open while the fourth, made of glass, is the entrance to the hall.

facts.fact: It now hosts trade fairs, exhibitions, music festivals and open-air cinema.
facts.quote: While the Grande Halle is within Paris' main abattoir district, the historical building now serves as a venue for trade fairs, exhibitions, music festivals, and open-air cinema.

facts.fact: Genoa's Old Harbour was revitalised for the 1992 Columbus celebrations, largely to designs by Renzo Piano.
facts.quote: The Old Harbour (Porto Antico) area was revitalised for the 1992 Columbian Celebrations, largely to the designs of Genoese architect Renzo Piano.

facts.fact: Piano designed the Biosphere, known as 'Piano's bubble', a glass sphere housing a tropical ecosystem, as well as the Bigo panoramic lift.
facts.quote: Piano also designed the Bigo, a panoramic lift, and the Biosphere (known as "Piano's bubble"), a glass sphere housing a tropical ecosystem.

facts.fact: Piano's programme turned the run-down industrial port into a cultural centre and added a botanical garden in a glass dome.
facts.quote: Piano also carried out a large program for revitalization of the old port of Genoa to transform it from a rundown industrial area into a cultural center and tourist attraction. He prolonged streets to give access to the port, transformed old port buildings into cultural and commercial buildings, added a library, an aquarium and an auditorium, a botanical garden in glass dome and a giant multi-armed crane, modeled after the old cranes of the port, which hoists visitors high in the air for a view of the port.

facts.fact: Sam Stephenson was chosen in 1965 to design the Central Bank on Dame Street because he had stood up to conservationists over the ESB Headquarters.
facts.quote: When he was chosen to design the new Central Bank of Ireland, Dame Street in 1965 it was because of how he had stood up to conservationists during the construction of the controversial ESB Headquarters on Fitzwilliam Street.

facts.fact: The bank (1975) was built higher than planning permission allowed; this was put right afterwards, and the matter was debated in the Oireachtas in 1974.
facts.quote: Central Bank of Ireland Dame Street (1975) - It was built higher than planning permission allowed but this was rectified retrospectively. The matter was debated in the Oireachtas in 1974.

facts.fact: Stephenson's best-known buildings are all in Dublin and are examples of Brutalist architecture.
facts.quote: Stephenson's most famous buildings are all in Dublin, and exemplify the style of Brutalist architecture.

facts.fact: Blenheim Palace is a country house in Woodstock, Oxfordshire, the seat of the Dukes of Marlborough and Winston Churchill's birthplace.
facts.quote: Blenheim Palace ( BLEN-im) is a country house in Woodstock, Oxfordshire, England. It is the seat of the Dukes of Marlborough, and the birthplace of Sir Winston Churchill.

facts.fact: One of England's largest houses, it was built between 1705 and 1722 and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
facts.quote: One of England's largest houses, it was built between 1705 and 1722, and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

facts.fact: It was meant as the nation's reward to the 1st Duke of Marlborough for his victory at the Battle of Blenheim in 1704.
facts.quote: The palace is named after the 1704 Battle of Blenheim. It was originally intended to be a reward to the 1st Duke of Marlborough for his military triumphs against the French and Bavarians in the War of the Spanish Succession, which culminated in the eponymous battle near the town of Blenheim in what is today southern Germany.

facts.fact: It is designed in the rare, short-lived English Baroque style, and opinion on it is still divided.
facts.quote: Designed in the rare, and short-lived, English Baroque style, the palace elicits architectural assessments as divided today as they were in the 1720s.

facts.fact: John Vanbrugh, a dramatist with no architectural training, usually worked with the trained Nicholas Hawksmoor; the pair had just begun Castle Howard.
facts.quote: Vanbrugh, a popular dramatist, was an untrained architect, who usually worked in conjunction with the trained and practical Nicholas Hawksmoor. The duo had recently completed the first stages of the Baroque Castle Howard.

facts.fact: Vanbrugh planned the house to be seen in perspective, from a distance; the site covers about seven acres.
facts.quote: Vanbrugh planned Blenheim in perspective; that is, to be best viewed from a distance. As the site covers some seven acres (2.8 hectares), this is also a necessity.

facts.fact: To look monumental, Vanbrugh used a severe Baroque, with great masses of stone suggesting strength and casting shadow as decoration.
facts.quote: To create this monumental effect, Vanbrugh chose to design in a severe Baroque style, using great masses of stone to imitate strength and create shadow as decoration.
