facts.fact: The main block and two service blocks form the Great Court, designed to overpower arriving visitors.
facts.quote: The three blocks together form the "Great Court" designed to overpower the visitor arriving at the palace.

facts.fact: Áras an Uachtaráin, formerly the Viceregal Lodge, is the official residence and main workplace of the president of Ireland.
facts.quote: Áras an Uachtaráin (Irish pronunciation: [ˈaːɾˠəsˠ ənˠ ˈuəxt̪ˠəɾˠaːnʲ] ; "Residence of the President"), formerly the Viceregal Lodge, is the official residence and principal workplace of the president of Ireland.

facts.fact: It stands in Dublin's Phoenix Park; its design is credited to amateur architect Nathaniel Clements, probably guided by professionals, and it was completed around 1751–1757.
facts.quote: The estate is located off Chesterfield Avenue in the Phoenix Park in Dublin, with the building's design being credited to amateur architect Nathaniel Clements but more likely guided by professionals (John Wood of Bath, Sir Edward Lovett Pearce and Richard Cassels) and completed around 1751 to 1757.

facts.fact: Clements, Chief Ranger of the Phoenix Park, built the ranger's lodge to his own design in 1751.
facts.quote: Clements was appointed by King George II to the office of Chief Ranger of the Phoenix Park and Master of Game and built the Ranger's lodge (subsequently the Viceregal Lodge) to his own design in 1751.

facts.fact: The Crown bought it in the 1780s as the summer residence of the Lord Lieutenant of Ireland.
facts.quote: It was bought by the Crown in the 1780s to become the summer residence of the Lord Lieutenant of Ireland, the British viceroy in the Kingdom of Ireland.

facts.fact: In 1911 the house was greatly extended for the visit of King George V and Queen Mary.
facts.quote: In 1911, the house underwent a large extension for the visit of King George V and Queen Mary.

facts.fact: The Second World War saved the building from planned demolition, and by 1945 it was too closely tied to the presidency to be pulled down.
facts.quote: The outbreak of the Second World War saved the building, which had been renamed Áras an Uachtaráin (meaning house or residence of the president in Irish), from demolition, as plans for its demolition and the design of a new residence were put on hold. By 1945 it had become too closely identified with the presidency of Ireland to be demolished, though its poor condition meant that extensive demolition and rebuilding of parts of the building were necessary, notably the kitchens, servants' quarters and chapel.

facts.fact: Some historians claim its garden-front portico was a model for the White House, but the White House porticoes were added later by Latrobe.
facts.quote: Some historians have claimed that the garden front portico of Áras an Uachtaráin (which can be seen by the public from the main road through the Phoenix Park) was used as a model by Irish architect James Hoban, who designed the White House in Washington, D.C. However, the porticoes were not part of Hoban's original design and were, in fact, added to the White House at a later date by Benjamin Henry Latrobe.

facts.fact: Chichester Festival Theatre is a Grade II* listed theatre in Oaklands Park, Chichester.
facts.quote: Chichester Festival Theatre is a theatre and Grade II* listed building situated in Oaklands Park in the city of Chichester, West Sussex, England.

facts.fact: Designed by Philip Powell and Hidalgo Moya, it was opened in 1962 by its founder Leslie Evershed-Martin.
facts.quote: Designed by Philip Powell and Hidalgo Moya, it was opened by its founder Leslie Evershed-Martin in 1962.

facts.fact: Evershed-Martin modelled the idea on the Stratford Festival in Stratford, Ontario.
facts.quote: Leslie Evershed-Martin drew parallels between Chichester and the Canadian city of Stratford, Ontario, and concluded that Chichester could sustain a theatre similar to the Stratford Festival.

facts.fact: Laurence Olivier was its first artistic director, and the first National Theatre company was formed there.
facts.quote: The inaugural artistic director was Sir Laurence Olivier, and it was at Chichester that the first National Theatre company was formed.

facts.fact: The smaller Minerva Theatre was built nearby in 1989.
facts.quote: The smaller and more intimate Minerva Theatre was built nearby in 1989.

facts.fact: Powell and Moya also designed the Skylon, Churchill Gardens and the Museum of London.
facts.quote: Among other projects, Powell and Moya designed Chichester Festival Theatre, the Skylon (the landmark structure of the 1951 Festival of Britain), Churchill Gardens in Pimlico, Northbrooks in Harlow, St Paul's School, London, the Museum of London, Christ Church Picture Gallery, Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

facts.fact: The Bord Gáis Energy Theatre, first called the Grand Canal Theatre, is in Dublin's Docklands and is Ireland's largest fixed-seat theatre.
facts.quote: The Bord Gáis Energy Theatre (originally the Grand Canal Theatre) is a performing arts venue, located in the Docklands of Dublin, Ireland. It is Ireland's largest fixed-seat theatre.

facts.fact: Daniel Libeskind designed it for the Dublin Docklands Development Authority, and it opened on 18 March 2010.
facts.quote: It was designed by Daniel Libeskind for the DDDA, built by Joe O'Reilly (Chartered Land), and opened by Harry Crosbie on 18 March 2010.

facts.fact: The site was once part of the Dublin Gasworks, demolished in 1985 and later decontaminated at a cost of over €50M.
facts.quote: The site originally housed various buildings and structures of the Dublin Gasworks Company which were demolished in 1985 and decontaminated by the DDDA in the late 1990s and early 2000s at a cost of over €50M.

facts.fact: It has 2,111 seats and is the only Irish theatre whose stage can host major West End shows.
facts.quote: Grand Canal Theatre (13,765 ext. / 10,882 int. square metres, 2,111 seats) is the largest fixed seated theatre in Ireland, and the only Irish theatre with a stage capable of hosting major London West-End shows.

facts.fact: Libeskind's studio also designed the office blocks on either side so the scheme would be integrated.
facts.quote: Studio Liebskind also designed the office blocks on either side of the theatre (2, 4 & 5 Grand Canal Square) to ensure O'Reilly's scheme was integrated.

facts.fact: It was built from January 2007 to late 2009, with John Sisk & Sons as contractor and Arup as engineers.
facts.quote: Construction started on the theatre in January 2007 and finished in late 2009. The main contractor was John Sisk & Sons and Arup were the main engineers.

facts.fact: Martha Schwartz's 'red carpet' piazza in front was designed to tie in with the theatre.
facts.quote: The DDDA's wider development of the Grand Canal Square (Grand Canal Dock regeneration project), included another office block (1 Grand Canal Square at 11,600 m2 or 125,000 sq ft, completed in 2007), a 5-star Hotel (the Manuel Aires Mateus designed, Marker Hotel, completed in 2012 but to a lower specification) and a Martha Schwartz designed 930-square-metre (10,000 sq ft) central piazza (on a "red carpet" theme, integrating with the Liebskind theatre, completed in 2008).

facts.fact: The Ames Free Library in Easton, Massachusetts, is a public library designed by H. H. Richardson, next to his Oakes Ames Memorial Hall.
facts.quote: The Ames Free Library is a public library designed by noted American architect Henry Hobson Richardson. It is located at 53 Main Street, Easton, Massachusetts, immediately adjacent to another Richardson building, Oakes Ames Memorial Hall.

facts.fact: Oliver Ames Jr. left $50,000 in his will for a library, to be private but run in trust for the public.
facts.quote: On the death of Oliver Ames Jr., he left $50,000 for the construction of a library. The will stipulated that it was to be a private institution, not owned by the town, but operated in trust for the public.

facts.fact: It was built from 1877 to 1879 but opened only on 10 March 1883.
facts.quote: The library was built from 1877 to 1879, although it did not open until March 10, 1883.

facts.fact: The façade is light-brown Milford granite in random ashlar with reddish-brown Longmeadow brownstone trim, under a red-orange tile roof.
facts.quote: The facade is light-brown Milford granite laid in random ashlar with reddish-brown Longmeadow brownstone trim. Its roof is red-orange tile.

facts.fact: The gable front has a heavily arched entry and, above it, five arched windows separated by pairs of short columns.
facts.quote: The gable's front facade contains a heavily arched entry on the first floor and a row of five arched windows separated by pairs of short columns above.

facts.fact: Inside, the stack wing, hall and reading room run lengthwise; the reading room fireplace is mainly by Stanford White and the medallions by Augustus Saint-Gaudens.
facts.quote: Within, the library's major rooms, stack wing, hall, and reading room are laid out longitudinally. The reading room's fireplace is primarily by Stanford White, and the stone and bronze medallions of Oliver Ames Jr. were designed by Augustus Saint-Gaudens.

facts.fact: It belongs to Richardson's series of small New England town libraries that defines his style.
facts.quote: A series of small public libraries donated by patrons for the improvement of New England towns makes a small coherent corpus that defines Richardson's style: Winn Memorial Library (Woburn), Ames Free Library (Easton), the Converse Memorial Library (Malden), and the Thomas Crane Public Library (Quincy), (1880–1882) "generally regarded by architectural historians as the masterpiece of Richardson's libraries", the Hubbard Memorial Library (Ludlow, Massachusetts), and Billings Memorial Library on the campus of the University of Vermont.

facts.fact: The Campbell Sports Center, part of Columbia University's Baker Field Athletics Complex, was designed by Steven Holl with senior partner Chris McVoy.
facts.quote: The Campbell Sports Center, a Columbia University's Baker Field Athletics Complex, is designed by Steven Holl and senior partner Chris McVoy.

facts.fact: On the corner of West 218th Street and Broadway, it is meant as a new gateway to the Baker Athletics Complex.
facts.quote: Sited on the corner of West 218th street and Broadway, the Campbell Sports Center aims to form an inviting new gateway to the Baker Athletics Complex, the primary athletics facility for the University’s outdoor sports program.

facts.fact: The design idea, 'points on the ground, lines in space', comes from field-play diagrams and grows from point foundations on the sloping site.
facts.quote: Steven Holl Architects' design concept for the building is based on "points on the ground, lines in space," which refers to field play diagrams used for football, soccer, baseball, and develops from point foundations on the sloping site.

facts.fact: External stairs and terraces link the building to the fields below and give views over the complex and Manhattan.
facts.quote: External stairs and terraces along the facade connect the building with the athletic fields below, giving views from the upper levels over the Baker Athletics Complex and Manhattan.

facts.fact: The five-storey, 48,000 sq ft building opened in fall 2012, with training spaces, offices, an auditorium and study rooms.
facts.quote: The five story, 48,000sf facility, which opened in Fall 2012, houses strength and conditioning spaces, offices for varsity sports, an auditorium, a hospitality suite and student-athlete study rooms.

facts.fact: Michael Kimmelman of The New York Times called it 'not a beauty' but 'tough, sophisticated and imaginative' for a devilish site.
facts.quote: Michael Kimmelman of The New York Times called it "not a beauty. But it is a tough, sophisticated and imaginative work of architecture for a devilish site."

facts.fact: Completed in 1966, the fifteen-storey Crawford Manor is a significant mature work of Paul Rudolph and a local example of Brutalism.
facts.quote: Completed in 1966, the fifteen-story building is a significant mature work of architect Paul Rudolph, and a good local example of Brutalist architecture.

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2015 and is used by the city for public housing.
facts.quote: The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2015, and as a non-contributing element to the Dwight Street Historic District in 1983. It is owned by the city of New Haven, which uses it for public housing.

facts.fact: It has a steel frame and concrete blocks with a rusticated concrete finish, on an irregular C-shaped footprint.
facts.quote: The building is fifteen stories in height, with an irregular C-shaped footprint. The building is built with a steel frame and concrete blocks, and is finished with a rusticated concrete finish.

facts.fact: Full-height windowless piers separate the windows and porches from each other.
facts.quote: Full-height windowless piers separate other visual elements, including windows and porches, from each other.

facts.fact: Inside, ribbed rough concrete matches the exterior, and there are 109 studio or one-bedroom units.
facts.quote: The interior is finished in a manner similar to the exterior, with ribbed rough concrete elements, and poured concrete floors and ceilings. It now houses 109 units, either studio or single bedrooms.

facts.fact: Begun in 1964 as housing for needy senior citizens, it was designed by Rudolph while he headed the Yale School of Architecture.
facts.quote: Construction on Crawford Manor was begun in 1964, in order to address a well-documented shortage of public housing for needy senior citizens. It was designed by Paul Rudolph, then the head of the Yale University School of Architecture, and a well-known advocate of what has since been called Brutalist architecture.

facts.fact: In Learning from Las Vegas (1972), Venturi and Scott Brown called Crawford Manor a 'duck', 'heroic and original', against their 'decorated shed'.
facts.quote: They thus label Crawford Manor a duck, "heroic and original," while their Guild House (1963) is a decorated shed, "ugly and ordinary."

facts.fact: The Wiesner Building was designed by I. M. Pei & Partners and dedicated in 1985.
facts.quote: It was designed by I.M. Pei & Partners. It is named in honor of former MIT president Jerome Wiesner and his wife Laya and was dedicated in 1985.

facts.fact: It houses the MIT Media Lab and the List Visual Arts Center.
facts.quote: The Wiesner building (Building E15) houses the MIT Media Lab and the List Visual Arts Center and is named in honor of former MIT president Jerome Wiesner and his wife Laya.

facts.fact: The building is very box-like, a motif repeated inside and out, like boxes packed within each other.
facts.quote: The building is very box-like, a motif that is consistently repeated in both the interior and exterior design evoking a sense of boxes packed within each other.

facts.fact: It is notable for close collaboration between architect and artists, and its flat, gridded skin of white modular metal panels sets it apart.
facts.quote: The building is notable for the level of collaboration between the architect and artists. It stands apart from the surrounding neighborhood with its flat, gridded skin make of white, modular metal panels.

facts.fact: Kenneth Noland designed the exterior as a metaphor of technology, like graph paper and number grids.
facts.quote: The building's exterior, designed by Kenneth Noland, is meant as a metaphor of technology through the grids of graph paper and number matrices while also quoting the corridor-like morphology of the rest of the MIT campus.

facts.fact: Scott Burton, Alan Shields and Richard Fleischner worked on the inner atria and the landscaping.
facts.quote: Scott Burton, Alan Shields, and Richard Fleischner also collaborated extensively in the final design of the internal atria and external landscaping.

facts.fact: Edmonton City Hall, home of the city government, was designed by Dub Architects and completed in 1992.
facts.quote: The Edmonton City Hall is the home of the municipal government of Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. Designed by Dub Architects, the building was completed in 1992.

facts.fact: It has two steel-and-glass pyramids on a three-storey concrete base; one lights the main atrium, the other the council chamber.
facts.quote: The building features two steel and glass pyramids, one 43 metres (141 ft) (ground to peak), on top of a three-storey concrete structure. One pyramid provides natural light for the main atrium, the other for the council chambers.

facts.fact: A 60-metre clock tower, the Friendship Tower, carries 23 carillon bells.
facts.quote: The building also features a 60-metre-high (200 ft) clock (Friendship Tower) topped with a set of 23-carillon bells.

facts.fact: It is the main feature of Sir Winston Churchill Square, whose fountain becomes a skating rink in winter.
facts.quote: Located on the eastern edge of the financial district in Edmonton's downtown, the building is the main feature on Sir Winston Churchill Square. In the winter, the fountain is converted to a skating rink.

facts.fact: The first design had four cones evoking First Nations tipis, but the public disliked them.
facts.quote: The cones were meant to evoke the tipis that the First Nations once lived in on the site. The design met with negative feedback from the public as they felt the cones looked like dunce caps and nuclear reactors.

facts.fact: The cones became pyramids meant to recall the Rocky Mountains and the Muttart Conservatory.
facts.quote: Dub Architects then revised their design to replace the cones with pyramids, with the pyramids designed to be evocative of the Rocky Mountains and the Muttart Conservatory.

facts.fact: Rogers Centre, originally SkyDome, is a retractable-roof stadium at the base of the CN Tower in Toronto, opened in 1989.
facts.quote: Rogers Centre (originally SkyDome) is a retractable roof stadium in downtown Toronto, Ontario, Canada, situated at the base of the CN Tower near the northern shore of Lake Ontario. Opened in 1989 on the former Railway Lands, it is home to the Toronto Blue Jays of Major League Baseball (MLB).

facts.fact: It was the first stadium with a fully retractable motorised roof and has a 348-room hotel, 70 rooms of which overlook the field.
facts.quote: The venue is noted for being the first stadium to have a fully retractable motorized roof, as well as for the 348-room hotel attached to it with 70 rooms overlooking the field.

facts.fact: It was designed by architect Rod Robbie and structural engineer Michael Allen, and built from October 1986 to May 1989.
facts.quote: The stadium was designed by architect Rod Robbie and structural engineer Michael Allen and was constructed by the EllisDon Construction company of London, Ontario and the Dominion Bridge Company of Lachine, Quebec. The stadium's construction lasted about 2+1⁄2 years, from October 1986 to May 1989.

facts.fact: The Robbie/Allen scheme won the 1985 competition because it had the largest roof opening and was the most technically sound.
facts.quote: Ultimately, the Robbie/Allen concept won because it provided the largest roof opening of all the finalists, and it was the most technically sound.

facts.fact: The 31-storey-high roof has four panels: one fixed, three moved by electric 'train' engines on railway rails.
facts.quote: The 31-storey-high roof consists of four panels: one (on the north end) is fixed in place and the other three are moved by electrically driven 'train' engines, that run on high-strength railway rails.

facts.fact: The roof, of steel trusses with corrugated steel and a PVC membrane, takes 20 minutes to open.
facts.quote: The roof, which takes 20 minutes to open, was made out of steel trusses covered by corrugated steel cladding, which in turn is covered by a single-ply PVC membrane.

facts.fact: The two middle panels slide over the fixed north panel, then the south panel rotates round and nests inside the stack.
facts.quote: The two middle panels slide laterally to stack over the north semi-circular panel (which is fixed in place), and then the south semi-circular panel rotates around the stadium and nests inside the stack.

facts.fact: Robbie and Allen's patented design proved that multi-use retractable-roof stadiums could work and revived the downtown stadium in North America.
facts.quote: Robbie and Allen’s patented winning design established the viability of multi-use retractable roofed stadiums worldwide and lead to a renaissance of the idea of the downtown stadium across North America.

facts.fact: The Tuschinski is a cinema near Rembrandtplein in Amsterdam.
facts.quote: The Koninklijk Theater Tuschinski (English: Royal Theatre Tuschinski) also called Pathé Tuchinski, is a movie theatre in Amsterdam, Netherlands, near Rembrandtplein and belonging to the historic French group Pathé.

facts.fact: Construction began on 18 June 1919, mixing Art Deco, Jugendstil and Amsterdam School styles, at about 4 million guilders.
facts.quote: Construction started on 18 June 1919, the theatre was built in Art Deco, Jugendstil and the Amsterdams School style at a cost of circa ƒ 4 million.

facts.fact: Its electro-technical features were considered revolutionary, and its heating and ventilation system kept the whole building at an even temperature.
facts.quote: The theatre contained electro-technical features, then considered revolutionary. Its unique heating and ventilation system kept the temperature even throughout the building.

facts.fact: It was declared a national monument in 1967 for its distinctive architecture.
facts.quote: The site was declared a national monument in 1967 due to its distinctive architecture.

facts.fact: The western façade is flanked by two towers and decorated with ceramic sculptures and leaded windows.
facts.quote: The western facade is flanked by two towers. It is decorated with ceramic sculptures and contains several leadlight windows.

facts.fact: The building has Asian influences, and the lobby was designed to make visitors feel they are stepping into an illusion.
facts.quote: The building contains Asian influences while the lobby was designed in a way to offer theatergoers the feeling that they are stepping into an illusion.

facts.fact: Pathé renovated it from 1998 to 2002 back to its original style.
facts.quote: They renovated the cinema from 1998 to 2002 to its original style and a corridor was constructed to Tuschinski 3, giving the complex a total of 6 auditoriums.

facts.fact: At its centenary in 2021, Time Out named Tuschinski the most beautiful cinema in the world.
facts.quote: During the centennial Time Out magazine named Tuschinski the most beautiful cinema in the world.

facts.fact: Müpa Budapest, the Palace of Arts, opened in March 2005 near Rákóczi Bridge and was designed by Zoboki, Demeter and Partners.
facts.quote: Müpa Budapest (between 2005 and 2015 Palace of Arts – Művészetek Palotája in Hungarian [ˈmyːveːsɛtɛk ˈpɒlotaːjɒ]) is a building in Ferencváros, Budapest, Hungary, officially opened in March 2005. It is located near Rákóczi Bridge and was designed by Zoboki, Demeter and Partners Architectural Office.

facts.fact: It covers 10,000 m² of ground with 70,000 m² of floor, and its concert hall, Festival Theatre and Ludwig Museum were built together in 28 months.
facts.quote: The structure of Müpa Budapest covers a ground area of 10,000 m2 and the total floor space of the building is 70,000 m2. Its three institutions, the concert hall, the Festival Theatre and the Ludwig Museum, were built in parallel over 28 months.

facts.fact: It won FIABCI's Prix d'Excellence in 2006.
facts.quote: It received the Prix d’Excellence of FIABCI in 2006.

facts.fact: The Bartók National Concert Hall is 25 m high, 25 m wide and 52 m long and seats 1,656.
facts.quote: Bartók National Concert Hall is 25 m high, 25 m wide and 52 m long, and seats 1,656 people, including 126 seats on the podium and 60 standing places in the side galleries.

facts.fact: Its acoustics can be tuned with 58 movable resonance chambers and a suspended 42-tonne canopy.
facts.quote: The acoustics can be adjusted with 58 movable resonance chambers and a suspended 42-tonne canopy.

facts.fact: The concert hall's organ, built by Orgelbau Mühleisen with the Pécs Organ Building Manufactory, is one of the largest in Europe.
facts.quote: It was built by the German firm Orgelbau Mühleisen together with the Pécs Organ Building Manufactory. It is one of the largest organs in Europe.

facts.fact: It stands next to the National Theatre as part of Budapest's new Millennium City Center.
facts.quote: Both Müpa Budapest and the National Theatre are part of the new Millennium City Center being created in Budapest.

facts.fact: Baan Dam, the Black House, is a private art museum by Thawan Duchanee mixing traditional northern Thai buildings with unconventional contemporary architecture.
facts.quote: Baandam Museum (Thai: พิพิธภัณฑ์บ้านดำ, RTGS: ban dam, lit. 'black house'), also known in English as the Black House Museum, is a private art museum comprising a mixture of traditional northern Thai buildings with unconventional and contemporary architecture, designed by Thawan Duchanee.

facts.fact: The museum covers about 160,000 square metres with over 40 structures spread across the site.
facts.quote: The museum covers an area of about 160,000 square meters, consisting of over 40 different structures scattered around the site.

facts.fact: The Cathedral, the main art building, was designed by Thawan Duchanee and built by Baan Dam's own engineers in 1999–2009.
facts.quote: The Cathedral (Art Museum Building; Thai: มหาวิหาร), was  designed by Thawan Duchanee and built by Baan Dam's engineers in 1999 - 2009.

facts.fact: The Cathedral is a wooden building on 44 large pillars, raised about 2.8 metres on brick.
facts.quote: The cathedral is a large single-story rectangular building with an east-west alignment, raised from the ground about 2.8 meters on brick. The structure is wood with Thai style decor named Bua pattern at the base each of 44 large wooden pillars.

facts.fact: Its roof is steeply pitched in four Lanna-style tiers, covered with unglazed clay tiles.
facts.quote: The roof is steeply pitched with four-tiers in Lanna style covered with unglazed clay tiles and decorated with Thai and Lanna features such as swan tail (Thai:หางหงส์), balalee (Thai:บราลี), tiered (Thai:ฉัตร), and  There are three large doors at the east and west ends with stairs leading up to them.

facts.fact: The east pavilion uses glass in place of walls under a Lanna-style mansard roof.
facts.quote: The east pavilion uses glass instead of a wall, and has a triangular mansard Lanna style roof covered with indigenous terracotta tiles.

facts.fact: The Cathay Building was designed by British architect Frank W. Brewer, planned at 16 storeys but completed with 11.
facts.quote: The supposed 16 storey (11 storey upon completion) Cathay Building was designed by British architect Frank W Brewer.

facts.fact: It was Singapore's first skyscraper and the tallest building in Southeast Asia at the time.
facts.quote: Cathay Building was the first skyscraper in Singapore and tallest building in Southeast Asia at that time.

facts.fact: It held the Cathay Cinema, a restaurant and a dance hall on the ground floor, with a roof garden over the cinema and a residential block with a penthouse.
facts.quote: The Cathay Building consisted of the Cathay Cinema, a restaurant and the dance hall on the ground floor, as well as a roof garden above the cinema and a residential storey block with a penthouse.

facts.fact: The cinema opened on 3 October 1939 and the 11-storey residential block on 1 July 1940.
facts.quote: The first part of the Cathay Building was opened on 3 October 1939 with the 1,300-seat Cathay Cinema, the dance hall and the Cathay Restaurant. On 1 July 1940, the 11 storey residential block was opened for occupancy, with the owners Mrs Loke Yew and Loke Wan Tho occupied the eleventh floor.

facts.fact: Its theatre was the island's first air-conditioned cinema and public building.
facts.quote: Its theatre was the island's first air-conditioned cinema and public building, and where one could sit in an arm chair to watch a film; a rare amenity during that time.

facts.fact: Subhas Chandra Bose announced the Provisional Government of Free India there on 21 October 1943.
facts.quote: On 21 October 1943, Subhas Chandra Bose announced the formation of the Provisional Government of Azad Hind (Free India) at Cathay Building with himself as the Head of State, Prime Minister and Minister of War.

facts.fact: It was almost completely demolished, keeping only part of the main façade; it was gazetted a national monument on 10 February 2003, the first demolished building to be so.
facts.quote: The building was nearly completely demolished, with only a small portion of the main facade, which had been covered up for decades, was revealed and preserved. This was the first demolished building to be gazetted as a national monument on 10 February 2003 while it retains a significant heritage value.

facts.fact: Atarim Square is a complex of buildings and a public square in Tel Aviv, designed by Yaakov Rechter.
facts.quote: Atarim Square (also  Namir Square) is a complex of buildings and a public square in Tel Aviv, Israel, designed by architect Yaakov Rechter.

facts.fact: It is an example of Brutalist architecture in Israel.
facts.quote: It is an example of Brutalist architecture in Israel.

facts.fact: It was planned as a tourist centre linking the new beachfront hotels, the beaches and Sderot Ben-Gurion.
facts.quote: It was decided to develop the square as a tourist center to connect the hotels, beaches and Sderot Ben-Gurion, and planned to include a main road parallel to the shore and parking lot.

facts.fact: Begun in 1971, the multi-purpose structure steps down several levels to use the drop of the cliff to the beach.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1971. The multi-purpose structure was built on a number of levels which exploited the difference in elevations between the cliff where the beach was.

facts.fact: Parking sits at the bottom, a covered road above, then shops, and the roof forms the square with restaurants, an amphitheatre and a glass rotunda.
facts.quote: The lower level includes a parking lot and gas station. The level above includes a covered highway (Eliezer Peri Street). Two levels above sea level consists of indoor shops and the top level (roof structure) forms a square, including a number of restaurants, an amphitheater and a rotunda coated with glass (formerly known as Colosseum Club ).

facts.fact: The square opened in June 1975.
facts.quote: The square was inaugurated in June 1975.

facts.fact: Rechter worked in a Brutalist palette of exposed raw concrete, unlike the white stucco of his father's generation.
facts.quote: In contrast to the sleek white stucco of the international style of his father and his fellow architects, in his early career Yaakov Rechter designed with a brutalist pallet, exposing the raw concrete surface of his projects.

facts.fact: The Chords Bridge is a side-spar cable-stayed bridge in Jerusalem designed by Santiago Calatrava, carrying the light rail's Red Line.
facts.quote: The Chords Bridge (Hebrew: גשר המיתרים, Gesher HaMeitarim), also called the Bridge of Strings or Jerusalem Light Rail Bridge, is a side-spar cable-stayed bridge in Jerusalem. The structure was designed by the Spanish architect and engineer Santiago Calatrava and is used by Jerusalem Light Rail's Red Line, which began service on August 19, 2011.

facts.fact: It includes a glass-sided footbridge, cost about $70 million and was inaugurated on 25 June 2008.
facts.quote: Incorporated in the bridge is a glass-sided pedestrian bridge enabling pedestrians to cross from Kiryat Moshe to the Jerusalem Central Bus Station. The bridge, which cost about $70 million (NIS 246 million), was inaugurated on June 25, 2008.

facts.fact: Like his Alamillo bridge in Seville, an angled cantilever tower takes some of the load and reduces the number of cables needed.
facts.quote: Similar to Calatrava's Puente del Alamillo in Seville, Spain, the bridge makes use of an angled cantilever tower to absorb some of the load and reduce the number of cable stays needed.

facts.fact: It was Calatrava's 40th bridge but his first to carry both trains and pedestrians.
facts.quote: While this is Calatrava's 40th bridge, it is the first he has designed to carry both train and pedestrian traffic.

facts.fact: A single 118-metre mast holds the deck with 66 steel cables in a three-dimensional parabolic shape; it was then Jerusalem's tallest structure.
facts.quote: A striking feature of the bridge is a single 118-metre (129 yd) high mast supporting the roadway via 66 steel cables arranged in a parabolic shape which develops three-dimensionally in space, making it the tallest structure in Jerusalem at the time of its completion.

facts.fact: It is mostly clad in Jerusalem stone, with steel, glass and concrete details.
facts.quote: The exterior of the bridge is mostly clad in Jerusalem stone, with steel, glass and concrete detailing.

facts.fact: Some see its form as a harp, with the cables as strings, symbolising King David's harp.
facts.quote: The form of the bridge resembles a tent in the desert or a harp, with the cables as the strings, symbolising King David's harp, according to some observers, others interpret the looming pylon as the bust of a long-necked bird, a human arm or an arrow caught in a bow.

facts.fact: It has been criticised as an extravagant, costly answer to a problem cheaper means could have solved.
facts.quote: Overall, however, the project has been criticized as an extravagant and costly solution to a problem that could have been solved by cheaper means.

facts.fact: The Royal Tank Museum in Amman opened on 29 January 2018 and holds about 110 tanks and armoured vehicles shown in chronological order.
facts.quote: The Royal Tank Museum (Arabic: متحف الدبابات الملكي) is a military museum in Amman, Jordan, inaugurated on January 29, 2018. Located next to the King Abdullah II Park in Al Muqabalain. The Royal Tank Museum spans an area of approximately 20,000 square meters and houses around 110 tanks and armored vehicles from Jordan, Arab nations, and foreign countries, displayed in chronological order.

facts.fact: The museum was designed by Jordanian architect Zaid Daoud.
facts.quote: The museum's design was created by Jordanian architect Zaid Daoud.

facts.fact: Its two levels form a square fort with four main pillars, inspired by the desert palaces of the Jordanian Badia and the form of a tank.
facts.quote: The Royal Tank Museum features a futuristic design, consisting of two levels shaped like a square fort with four main pillars. This design is inspired by the desert palaces found in the Jordanian Badia, symbolizing the actual power and durability of tanks while reflecting the general form of a tank itself.

facts.fact: A Cobra attack helicopter hangs under a central glass dome.
facts.quote: At the center of the building sits a glass dome from which a Cobra attack helicopter is suspended, representing the transition from Jordan's ancient heritage to the future.

facts.fact: It was built with a metal structure, woodwork, glass and fibreglass-reinforced concrete.
facts.quote: Various materials were used in the design of the museum during its construction, including a metal structure, woodwork, acoustic insulation, glass, and fiberglass-reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: It is a green building that stores water in a reservoir underneath and uses solar panels and LED lighting.
facts.quote: The museum is considered a green building, as it collects water in a large reservoir located beneath it for later reuse. Additionally, solar panels are installed to generate clean electrical energy, and special energy-saving lighting systems based on LED technology illuminate the interior of the museum.

facts.fact: Construction took nearly ten years.
facts.quote: Construction took nearly ten years, and it is managed by a Board of Trustees, which includes organizations such as the Greater Amman Municipality, the King Abdullah II Design and Development Bureau, the Royal Special Operations, and the Royal Automobile Museum.

facts.fact: The Brasília Planetarium opened on 15 March 1974, designed by Sérgio Bernardes in a Brutalist style.
facts.quote: Inaugurated on 15 March 1974, it was designed by architect Sérgio Bernandes using a Brutalist style.

facts.fact: It stands on the Monumental Axis in the Cultural Diffusion Sector, between the TV Tower and the Ulysses Guimarães Convention Center.
facts.quote: It is part of the Monumental Axis' Cultural Diffusion Sector (Portuguese: Setor de Difusão Cultural), being located between the Brasília TV Tower, the Ulysses Guimarães Convention Center, and near the Estádio Nacional Mané Garrincha and the Brasília Choro Club.

facts.fact: It closed in 2006 for repairs to structural problems and reopened on 11 December 2013.
facts.quote: In 2006, it was closed for refurbishing due to several structural problems, which lasted until 2013. It was reopened following construction work on 11 December 2013.

facts.fact: It is built of bare concrete in a geometric shape that looks like a flying saucer.
facts.quote: The planetarium was designed by architect Sérgio Bernandes, with a Brutalist architectural style, having bare concrete and a geometric shape resembling a flying saucer.

facts.fact: Its core is two half-spherical domes, one inside the other, ringed by sixteen identical volumes that form a sixteen-sided figure with concave sides.
facts.quote: Its center is formed by two semi-spherical domes, one inside the other, surrounded by sixteen identical volumes separated from each other by radial strips one meter thick, forming a hexadecagon with concave sides.

facts.fact: The sixteen faces stand for the sixteen points of the compass rose.
facts.quote: These volumes form sixteen faces, which represent the sixteen cardinal points of the compass rose.

facts.fact: Carrasco International Airport in Montevideo is Uruguay's main and largest airport.
facts.quote: Carrasco/General Cesáreo L. Berisso International Airport (IATA: MVD, ICAO: SUMU) is the main international airport of Uruguay. It is the country's largest airport and is located in the Carrasco neighborhood of Montevideo.

facts.fact: Work on the new terminal began on 3 February 2007, parallel to Runway 06/24.
facts.quote: On 3 February 2007, construction began on a new terminal parallel to Runway 06/24.

facts.fact: The new terminal was designed by Uruguayan architect Rafael Viñoly and handles 3 million passengers a year.
facts.quote: The new terminal, designed by Uruguayan architect Rafael Viñoly, has the capacity to handle 3 million passengers a year, including a much larger parking area built for over 1200 vehicles.

facts.fact: It has four jetways, separate floors for arrivals and departures and a large viewing area on the top floor.
facts.quote: This new terminal building has four jetways, separate floors for arrivals and departures and a large viewing area on the top floor.

facts.fact: It has room for two more jetways and up to 6 million passengers a year before it would need enlarging.
facts.quote: The terminal has room for expansion for two additional jetways and a maximum capacity of 6 million passengers per year before the building would need actual enlargement.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 5 October 2009 and began operating on 29 December 2009.
facts.quote: The new terminal was inaugurated on 5 October 2009 with official operations beginning on 29 December 2009.

facts.fact: The airport has been cited as one of the most efficient and traveller-friendly in Latin America.
facts.quote: It has been cited as one of the most efficient and traveler-friendly airports in Latin America.

facts.fact: The Comega Building stands at Avenida Corrientes 222, on the corner of Alem Avenue, in Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: The Comega Building is located on 222 Avenida Corrientes in the corner of Alem Avenue, in the city of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

facts.fact: It was Argentina's first reinforced concrete skyscraper and the first in Buenos Aires fully clad in travertine.
facts.quote: The Comega Building was the first reinforced concrete skyscraper built in Argentina and the first in Buenos Aires to show an exterior fully lined with travertine.

facts.fact: It was built in a rationalist style to a project by Alberto Stein with architects Enrique Douillet and Alfredo Joselevich.
facts.quote: It was built, in rationalist style, between 1921 and 1934 on a project by Ing. Alberto Stein and architects Enrique Douillet and Alfredo Joselevich.

facts.fact: Its five lifts were the first high-speed lifts in Buenos Aires, climbing 180 metres a minute.
facts.quote: A notable feature of the building was its five elevators, these being the first high-speed lifts of Buenos Aires, capable of climbing 180 meters per minute.

facts.fact: The unornamented, straight-edged exterior has two wings and a central tower of 21 floors and 88 metres around an open courtyard.
facts.quote: Its exterior has straight edges and is devoid of ornaments. It consists of two wings and a higher multi-storey central tower of 21 floors and 88 meters high. Together they surround a central open courtyard, facing Avenida Leandro N. Alem.

facts.fact: Inside, granite cladding and stainless steel counters were novel and costly for the time.
facts.quote: Its interior features granite cladding and stainless steel counters, which were considered extremely novel and expensive features for its time.

facts.fact: It is a declared architectural heritage of the city and has been renovated with many original features restored.
facts.quote: A declared architectural heritage of the city, the building has recently been renovated with much of its original features restored.

facts.fact: La Plata Cathedral is a Neo-Gothic church at the geographic centre of the city, facing Plaza Moreno and City Hall.
facts.quote: This Neogothic edifice is located in the geographical center of the city, facing the central square, Plaza Moreno, and the City Hall.

facts.fact: Inspired by Amiens and Cologne cathedrals, it was drawn by Ernesto Meyer under city planner Pedro Benoit.
facts.quote: Inspired by the European cathedrals of Amiens and Cologne, its plans were drawn by architect Ernesto Meyer under the direction of city planner Pedro Benoit.

facts.fact: The cornerstone was laid in 1884, and it became a cathedral in 1932.
facts.quote: The cornerstone was laid in 1884, and it was consecrated as the Parroquia Nuestra Señora de los Dolores in 1902. The parish church, which continued undergoing works, was designated a cathedral in 1932.

facts.fact: Work stopped in the 1930s for fear the foundations could not carry the planned weight, leaving the spires unfinished and the brick undressed.
facts.quote: In the 1930s, fearing that the foundation was insufficient for the projected size and weight of the structure, workers halted construction. The spires were left unfinished and the exterior brick work was left undressed.

facts.fact: The brick was left exposed after restoration, making it resemble the brick Gothic churches of northern Europe.
facts.quote: The building's exposed-brick exterior is thus unusual to some extent, and it makes La Plata Cathedral resemble the brick Gothic or Neogothic style of many churches in northern Europe, such as Uppsala Cathedral in Sweden, St. John's Church, Helsinki in Finland and Roskilde Cathedral in Denmark.

facts.fact: The completed and restored building was opened to the public in 2000.
facts.quote: The refurbishment was inaugurated to the public in the year 2000.

facts.fact: Its towers rise 112 metres, among the six tallest churches in the Americas.
facts.quote: With its towers rising 367 feet (112 m), it is among the six tallest churches in the Americas.

facts.fact: St. Augustine Cathedral stands on the Plaza de Armas of Talca and is the seat of the bishop of Talca.
facts.quote: It is located in the Plaza de Armas de Talca, and is the seat of the bishop of the Diocese of Talca in Chile.

facts.fact: Architect Ramón Venegas began it in 1938 on the site of the church destroyed by the 1928 Talca earthquake.
facts.quote: It was built by the architect Ramón Venegas and began in 1938 in the same place where the Mother Church was destroyed by the 1928 Talca earthquake.

facts.fact: It was consecrated on 30 September 1954.
facts.quote: It was finally consecrated on September 30, 1954.

facts.fact: The 2010 earthquake damaged its masonry walls and reinforced-concrete arches, putting it at risk of collapse.
facts.quote: The earthquake of 11 March 2010 left the temple with structural damage that included its walls of masonry and its arches of reinforced concrete, with risk of collapse.

facts.fact: Restoration finished in 2012, strengthening the walls with reinforced concrete and replacing the timber roof structure.
facts.quote: In 2012 the restoration work was completed, reinforcing the walls with reinforced concrete and replacing the wooden structure of the roof.

facts.fact: The Sunethra Bandaranaike House, or Horagolla Stables, is a country house renovated by Geoffrey Bawa in the 1980s.
facts.quote: The Sunethra Bandaranaike House or Horagolla Stables is the country house of Sunethra Bandaranaike, renovated in the 1980s by the renowned architect Geoffrey Bawa.

facts.fact: The building was the original walauwa of Horagolla, home of Sunethra Bandaranaike's great-grandfather.
facts.quote: The house was the original walauwa of Horagolla, the home of Sunethra Bandaranaike's great-grandfather Gate Mudaliyar Don Christoffel Henricus Dias Abeywickrema Jayatilake Seneviratne Bandaranaike.

facts.fact: Building work ran from 1 April 1983 to 25 November 1987.
facts.quote: Construction commenced on 1 April 1983 and was completed 25 November 1987.

facts.fact: The old stables and a new wing together form an L shape.
facts.quote: The building consists of two sections; the original stables and the new wing, with these two sections forming an 'L' shape.

facts.fact: New doors and windows were cut in, and a mezzanine splits the stable into a ground floor and an upper gallery.
facts.quote: Openings were introduced in the form of doors and windows and an internal mezzanine floor separates this space into a ground floor and upper gallery.

facts.fact: The horses' name boards were kept over their former stalls.
facts.quote: The name boards of the horses that were kept here have been retained over their former stalls.

facts.fact: It was built from recycled materials, taken from the original building or from old demolished houses.
facts.quote: The material used for the construction were recycled material sourced from either the original building or old demolished homes.

facts.fact: Singha Durbar, the 'Lion's Palace', is a palace in central Kathmandu built by Chandra Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana in 1908.
facts.quote: Singha Durbar (Nepali: सिंहदरबार, lit. 'Lion's Palace') is a palace in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal. The palace complex lies in the centre of Kathmandu, to the north of Babar Mahal and Thapathali Durbar and east of Bhadrakali Temple. This palace was built by Chandra Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana in June 1908.

facts.fact: It was designed by Kumar Narsingh Rana and Kishor Narsingh Rana.
facts.quote: The structure was designed by Kumar Narsingh Rana, Kishor Narsingh Rana.

facts.fact: Its architecture merges Palladian, Corinthian and Neoclassical traditions with Baroque.
facts.quote: The architecture of the palace is a unique example of merging building traditions, including Palladian, Corinthian, Neoclassical mansions along with Baroque architecture.

facts.fact: Before the 1973 fire it had 8 courtyards and 1,700 rooms with marble floors, painted ceilings and crystal lighting.
facts.quote: Before the fire of 1973, Singha Durbar had 8 courtyards and 1700 rooms with marbled floor, painted ceilings, silver furniture and expanses of crystal lighting.

facts.fact: The State Hall, the largest room, has Murano chandeliers, Belgian mirrors, English stained-glass doors and Italian marble floors.
facts.quote: This hall is adorned with foreign imported art pieces like Murano glass crystal chandeliers, Belgian mirrors along with English stained glass doors and Italian marble floors with floral patterns in walls and ceilings.

facts.fact: It houses Nepal's government offices, including the Federal Parliament.
facts.quote: It houses administrative offices of the Government of Nepal, including the Federal Parliament and several government ministries.

facts.fact: The main building was destroyed in the 2025 Gen Z protests.
facts.quote: In 2025, the main building was destroyed in the Gen Z protests, along with the prime minister's office.

facts.fact: The Alte Feste (Old Fortress) is a fortress and museum in central Windhoek, next to the Independence Memorial Museum.
facts.quote: The Alte Feste (English: Old Fortress) is a fortress and museum in downtown Windhoek, the capital of Namibia. It is situated in Robert Mugabe Avenue, next to the Independence Memorial Museum.

facts.fact: Captain Curt von François designed it as headquarters of the German colonial force in South West Africa.
facts.quote: The building was designed by captain Curt von François, in order to serve as headquarters of the imperial German Schutztruppe (colonial military force), during German colonization of South West Africa.

facts.fact: Its foundation was laid on 18 October 1890, and after several redesigns its final layout was completed in 1915.
facts.quote: The foundation was laid on 18 October 1890 by the then Schutztruppe private Gustav Tünschel. The building was redesigned multiple times during the first years; its final layout was only completed in 1915.

facts.fact: It has an inner courtyard with high walls, troop quarters inside, and four towers.
facts.quote: It consists of an inner courtyard with high walls and accommodation for the troops on the inside, as well as four towers.

facts.fact: It is the oldest surviving building in Windhoek, and the city grew up around it.
facts.quote: The Alte Feste is the oldest surviving building in the city which subsequently developed around it.

facts.fact: It was declared a National Monument in 1957 and extensively renovated in 1963.
facts.quote: Already severely dilapidated, it was declared a National Monument in 1957. The building was renovated extensively in 1963.

facts.fact: It holds the historic collection of the National Museum of Namibia, but as of 2023 it was closed and in urgent need of renovation.
facts.quote: The building today accommodates the historic collection of the National Museum of Namibia. As of 2023 Alte Feste is closed and in urgent need of renovation.

facts.fact: The arena opened in July 2025, replacing the Aichi Prefectural Gymnasium of 1964.
facts.quote: Opened in July 2025, the arena is a replacement for the Aichi Prefectural Gymnasium, which was built in 1964.

facts.fact: It was planned in 2017 after Aichi and Nagoya were chosen to host the 2026 Asian Games.
facts.quote: Aichi Prefectural Governor Hideaki Ōmura announced plans for the new arena in July 2017, almost a year after the prefecture and Nagoya city were unanimously selected to be the hosts of the 2026 Asian Games.

facts.fact: It was built in part of Meijō Park.
facts.quote: A section of Meijō Park north of the Aichi Prefectural Gymnasium was chosen to build the new arena.

facts.fact: Designed by Kengo Kuma, it seats up to 17,000.
facts.quote: Designed by Japanese architect Kengo Kuma, Aichi International Arena has a maximum seating capacity of 17,000.

facts.fact: It hosts Nagoya's annual grand sumo tournament every July.
facts.quote: The arena also hosts the annual grand sumo tournament that takes place in Nagoya every July.

facts.fact: Village Green is a large condominium complex that is both a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument and a National Historic Landmark.
facts.quote: Village Green consists of a large condominium complex that is both a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument and a National Historic Landmark.

facts.fact: Designed in the late 1930s and finished by 1942, it is one of the oldest planned communities of its type in the US.
facts.quote: Designed in the late 1930s and completed by 1942, it is one of the oldest planned communities of its type in the nation.

facts.fact: The AIA named it one of the 100 most important architectural achievements in US history.
facts.quote: Village Green was named by The American Institute of Architects as one of the 100 most important architectural achievements in U.S. history.

facts.fact: Its 627 units in a Modernist garden-city style were designed by Reginald D. Johnson with Clarence S. Stein, Wilson, Merrill & Alexander and landscape architect Fred Barlow Jr.
facts.quote: The Modernist Garden city style complex, which encompassed 627 units, was designed by architect Reginald D. Johnson, consulting architect Clarence S. Stein, with the firm of Wilson, Merill & Alexander, and landscape architect Fred Barlow Jr.

facts.fact: All roads and garages are kept to the edges of its eighty acres.
facts.quote: The development "was designed with all the roads and garages confined to the edges of its eighty-acre expanse."

facts.fact: At its centre is a long oval green crossed by paths, with smaller garden courts reaching out between the buildings.
facts.quote: At its center is an elongated oval greensward, lined and crossed by paved walkways. Smaller garden courts extend outward from the central area between the residence buildings.

facts.fact: The one- and two-storey plastered frame houses turn their living rooms and main bedrooms toward the gardens.
facts.quote: The residences are one or two story frame structures finished in plaster, with the living units organized so that the living room and master bedroom face one of the garden spaces.

facts.fact: The Cathedral Basilica of Lima, seat of the Archdiocese of Lima, was begun in 1535 and finished in 1797, built in its present form between 1602 and 1797.
facts.quote: It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Lima. Its construction began in 1535 by Francisco Pizarro and was completed in 1797, having been built in its present form between 1602 and 1797.

facts.fact: It stands on the eastern side of the Plaza Mayor in Lima's historic centre and is the oldest and largest church in Peru.
facts.quote: Located on the eastern limit of the Plaza Mayor, at the second block of the Jirón Carabaya, and is part of the Historic Centre of Lima. The Archbishop's Palace and Iglesia del Sagrario are located beside the cathedral. It is the oldest and largest church in Peru.

facts.fact: It was built on the site of the Inca shrine of Puma Inti and the palace of the prince Sinchi Puma.
facts.quote: The Cathedral of Lima was built on the site of the Inca shrine of the Puma Inti and the palace of the Cuscoan prince Sinchi Puma, a direct descendant of the Inca Sinchi Roca.

facts.fact: Francisco Becerra's plan, the basis of today's cathedral, took the cathedrals of Jaén and Seville partly as models.
facts.quote: Becerra made a new plan (considered to be the plan on which the existing cathedral is based) that took, in part, the cathedrals of Jaén and Seville as models.

facts.fact: Becerra's layout made a Renaissance church with a wide plan, three large naves and two side chapels.
facts.quote: The definitive layout of the cathedral, made by Becerra, resulted in a Renaissance-style church, with a wide floor plan and 3 large naves and two side chapels.

facts.fact: After earthquakes, chief architect Juan Martínez de Arrona argued for brick vaults while some councillors wanted a wooden roof.
facts.quote: Discussions were held on the best means of defense against seismic movements: the Chief Architect, Juan Martínez de Arrona, supported the idea of brick vaults, but several members of the Cabildo or Municipal Council considered that it would be better to cover the cathedral with wood.

facts.fact: In the reconstruction, the Jesuit Juan Rher used wood and quincha in the ribbed vaults and rebuilt the Renaissance stone doorway.
facts.quote: Rher took full advantage of the use of wood and quincha in the ribbed vaults, rebuilt the Renaissance stone doorway and advanced the work quite a bit, leaving the bell towers unfinished for a long time.

facts.fact: The present bell towers were rebuilt between 1794 and 1797 and finished by Matías Maestro.
facts.quote: Between the years 1794 and 1797 the current bell towers of the cathedral, which remained unfinished, were rebuilt being finished by the Presbyter Matías Maestro.

facts.fact: The Television Cultural Center (TVCC) is a skyscraper in Beijing's Central Business District with a hotel, a theatre and television studios.
facts.quote: The Television Cultural Center (TVCC; Chinese: 中央电视台电视文化中心) is a 34-story skyscraper on East Third Ring Road, Guanghua Road in the Central Business District (CBD) of Beijing, China. Featuring a hotel, a theater, and several television studios, the building was scheduled to open in mid-May 2009.

facts.fact: OMA won the contract for the CCTV Headquarters and the TVCC beside it on 20 December 2002.
facts.quote: The Office for Metropolitan Architecture won the contract from the Beijing International Tendering Co. to construct the CCTV Headquarters and the Television Cultural Center by its side on December 20, 2002.

facts.fact: The wedge-shaped building was designed by Rem Koolhaas and OMA, with Arup as engineers.
facts.quote: The innovative, wedge-shaped building was designed by the Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas and his firm Office for Metropolitan Architecture. The engineering firm for the building was Arup, East Asia, who designed and built the TVCC after an extensive internal study of the collapse of the World Trade Center on 11 September 2001.

facts.fact: Like the CCTV Headquarters, it used far less steel than ordinary skyscrapers and was designed to withstand major earthquakes.
facts.quote: The building, along with the CCTV Headquarters Building, was built using far less steel than conventional skyscrapers, and designed to withstand major earthquakes.

facts.fact: A continuous ground-floor lobby leads to a 1,500-seat theatre, a ballroom, digital cinemas, recording studios and exhibition spaces.
facts.quote: On the ground floor, a continuous lobby provides access to the 1500-seat theater, a large ballroom, digital cinemas, recording studios and exhibition facilities.

facts.fact: Hotel rooms line both sides of the tower, forming an atrium above the public facilities.
facts.quote: The hotel rooms occupy both sides of the tower, forming a spectacular atrium above the landscape of public facilities.

facts.fact: A major fire during construction delayed its opening until 16 May 2012.
facts.quote: Following a major fire during construction, however, the building's opening was delayed until 16 May 2012.

facts.fact: Completed in 2018 and used mostly for football, the main stadium was designed for 80,000 spectators.
facts.quote: It was completed in 2018, and it is used mostly for football matches. The main stadium was designed with a capacity of 80,000 spectators.

facts.fact: The stadium was built by NBBJ with CCDI on a 60,000 m² site on the Qiantang riverfront.
facts.quote: The stadium was built by NBBJ in partnership with CCDI. The stadium is built on a 60,000 square meters (650,000 sq ft) site on the Qiantang riverfront, opposite Hangzhou's Qianjiang New City Central Business District.

facts.fact: Its 80,800 seats are in three tiers, and the stands are opened on the north side to release heat and give views of the river.
facts.quote: There are 80,800 seats divided into three levels: upper, middle, and lower. The stands are disconnected on the north side to facilitate heat dissipation in the venue and allow spectators to enjoy the scenery of the Qiantang River.

facts.fact: The exterior draws on silk texture and the moving water of the Qiantang River.
facts.quote: The exterior design concept draws on the concepts of silk texture and dynamic Qiantang River water.

facts.fact: The outer shell is a steel structure of 28 large and 27 small petals.
facts.quote: The exterior is a steel structure with 28 large petals and 27 small petals.

facts.fact: The building covers 229,000 m², including 61,000 m² underground.
facts.quote: The construction area is 229,000 square meters (including 61,000 square meters of underground construction area).

facts.fact: Hangzhou hosted the 2022 Asian Games, including the men's football final.
facts.quote: Hangzhou hosted the 2022 Asian Games, with the men's football final and the 2022 Asian Para Games in September–October 2023.

facts.fact: The National Indoor Stadium seats 20,000 and was built for the 2008 Summer Olympics.
facts.quote: The stadium has a capacity of 20,000 people, and was constructed for the 2008 Summer Olympics.

facts.fact: It is nicknamed the Fan because its design resembles a traditional Chinese folding fan.
facts.quote: It is nicknamed the Fan (扇子, shànzi) due to its design resembling a traditional Chinese folding fan.

facts.fact: Glöckner³ designed it with the Beijing Institute of Architectural Design after winning an international competition in October 2003.
facts.quote: Glöckner³ designed the indoor stadium, in collaboration with the Beijing Institute of Architectural Design (BIAD), after winning an international architectural competition in October 2003.

facts.fact: Construction began in May 2005, and it opened on 26 November 2007.
facts.quote: Construction work began in May 2005. Before that, Cox Architecture were engaged as design consultants. The stadium opened its doors on November 26, 2007, for the artistic Gymnastics test event.

facts.fact: It was used for ice hockey at the 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympics.
facts.quote: The stadium was used for ice hockey during the 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympics.

facts.fact: The Temple in Independence, Missouri, is a house of worship and education 'dedicated to the pursuit of peace' at the Community of Christ's headquarters.
facts.quote: The Temple in Independence, Missouri, is a house of worship and education "dedicated to the pursuit of peace". It dominates the skyline of Independence and has become the focal point of the headquarters of the Community of Christ (formerly the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints).

facts.fact: Ground was broken on 6 April 1990 and it was dedicated on 17 April 1994.
facts.quote: Groundbreaking for the temple took place on April 6, 1990, and the completed structure was dedicated on April 17, 1994.

facts.fact: Gyo Obata's design evokes the spiral shell of the nautilus, with a stainless steel spire 300 feet high.
facts.quote: The temple was designed by Gyo Obata and evokes the spiral shell of the nautilus with a stainless steel spire that rises 300 feet (91 m).

facts.fact: A gently rising worshippers' path of textured stone spirals around the edge of the sanctuary.
facts.quote: This leads to the gently ascending worshipper's path of textured stone which spirals around its periphery.

facts.fact: The main sanctuary seats about 1,600 and has a Casavant pipe organ of 5,685 pipes.
facts.quote: The temple's main sanctuary has seating for approximately 1,600. It houses a Casavant pipe organ with 60 stops, 102 ranks, and 5685 pipes.

facts.fact: A large stained-glass wall of rice and wheat at the exit foyer won an AIA award for religious art.
facts.quote: At the exit foyer in the mouth of the spiral, "The Field is White, Already to Harvest" (see John: 4:35) is a large stained glass wall depicting rice and wheat, that earned an American Institute of Architects award for religious art.

facts.fact: The wide steps open onto a world plaza with a global map in inlaid brick.
facts.quote: The wide steps open up onto a world plaza with global map of inlaid brick.

facts.fact: The 63,000 sq ft Knight Building was designed by Coop Himmelb(l)au after an international competition, its first public project in the Americas.
facts.quote: The 63,000-square-foot (5,900 m2) John S. and James L. Knight Building was designed by the Viennese architectural firm Coop Himmelb(l)au following an international competition. The firm was chosen in part for its adaptive use of historic buildings, and the Knight Building is the firm's first public project in the Americas.

facts.fact: Ground was broken for the Knight Building on 22 May 2004.
facts.quote: Ground breaking for the new building was held on May 22, 2004.

facts.fact: The design joins new galleries, an auditorium and a café to the museum's 1899 building.
facts.quote: Coop Himmelb(l)au's design integrates additional gallery space, an auditorium and café with the museum's 1899 building utilizing contrasting, surprising and fanciful visual elements:

facts.fact: It has three parts: the 'Crystal' glass lobby, the 'Gallery Box', and the 'Roof Cloud', a 100-metre cantilevered steel-and-aluminium frame over old and new.
facts.quote: The "Crystal", a three-story glass lobby that serves as the public entry and as the focal visual space connecting the museum's artistic, educational, administrative, and public programming;	the "Gallery Box", comprising the Arnstein, Haslinger, Bidwell and Isroff Galleries, accommodates the museum's collection and temporary exhibitions; and the "Roof Cloud", a 327-foot (100 m)-long cantilevered steel and aluminum armature extends over the old and the new, creating a striking landmark for Akron's downtown which a critic once described as "a mechanical alligator snarfing down a Beaux Arts post office."

facts.fact: Wolf D. Prix said the design 'embraces the past, rather than replacing or destroying it'.
facts.quote: "The design embraces the past, rather than replacing or destroying it", said Coop Himmelb(l)au founder, and principal architect for the project, Wolf D. Prix.

facts.fact: Art since 1950 is shown in eight rooms of the Knight Building.
facts.quote: Art since 1950 is featured in eight rooms located in the museum's 2007 Knight building.

facts.fact: Vierzehnheiligen is a late Baroque (Rococo) basilica designed by Balthasar Neumann and built from 1743 to 1772.
facts.quote: The late Baroque (Rococo) basilica, designed by Balthasar Neumann, was constructed between 1743 and 1772.

facts.fact: It is dedicated to the Fourteen Holy Helpers, and its interior is nicknamed 'God's Ballroom'.
facts.quote: It is dedicated to the Fourteen Holy Helpers, a group of saints venerated together in the Catholic Church, especially in Germany at the time of the Black Death. The interior has been nicknamed "God's Ballroom".

facts.fact: It sits on a hillside above the river Main, facing Schloss Banz on the opposite hill.
facts.quote: The Basilica overlooks the river Main in Franconia. It sits on a hillside, and on the hillside opposite is Schloss Banz, a former Baroque abbey.

facts.fact: Langheim Abbey changed the plans to cut costs after the foundation stone was laid, and the apse walls were already up when Neumann found out.
facts.quote: Langheim Abbey wished for the costs of construction to be lowered and thus changed the architectural plans, despite the foundational stone already being laid. When this was discovered by Neumann, the architect, the walls of the three apses had already been erected.

facts.fact: Neumann split the space into three ovals so the Altar of Grace, fixed at the site of the apparitions, stands at the centre of the largest oval.
facts.quote: Neumann thus split the room into three ovals and placed the Altar back in the center by making it the center of the largest oval rotund in the middle, surrounded by four columns on each side.

facts.fact: The pulpit is carried by free-floating white putti.
facts.quote: Free-floating white putti bear the pulpit, ornamented with the golden reliefs of the Evangelists which are surrounded by shellwork.

facts.fact: Bergen Kunsthall is a contemporary art centre in Bergen that shows Norwegian and international artists.
facts.quote: Bergen Kunsthall is a contemporary art centre in Bergen, Norway, that organises and hosts exhibitions and events by both Norwegian and international artists.

facts.fact: It was founded in 1838 as Bergens Kunstforening and is housed in an early functionalist building designed in 1935 by Ole Landmark.
facts.quote: Bergen Kunsthall was originally founded in 1838 as Bergens Kunstforening, and is located in an early functionalist building designed in 1935 by the architect Ole Landmark.

facts.fact: It stands at Lille Lungegårdsvann in the centre of Bergen.
facts.quote: Other notable works include the Forum Kino at Kronstad and Bergen Kunsthall at Lille Lungegårdsvann in the center of Bergen.

facts.fact: Its 2017 exhibition by Charlotte Prodger won the 2018 Turner Prize.
facts.quote: Their 2017 exhibition "BRIDGIT" by Charlotte Prodger won the Turner Prize in 2018.

facts.fact: The Church of the Holy Spirit is a Lutheran church and parish centre in Wolfsburg, a notable work of Alvar Aalto.
facts.quote: Church of the Holy Spirit (German: Heilig Geist Kirche) is a Lutheran church and parish center in Wolfsburg, Germany. The building is a notable project of Finnish architect Alvar Aalto.

facts.fact: Pastor Erich Bammel commissioned Aalto personally in November 1958.
facts.quote: November 1958, Alvar Aalto was personally commissioned to design the church by then-pastor Erich Bammel; Aalto began designing the building the same year.

facts.fact: Construction started in 1961 and the church opened the following year.
facts.quote: The design was completed and construction started in 1961. The church opened the following year.

facts.fact: 2 Columbus Circle was designed by Edward Durell Stone in a modernist style for A&P heir Huntington Hartford, and Brad Cloepfil later redesigned it for the Museum of Arts and Design.
facts.quote: It was originally designed by Edward Durell Stone in the modernist style for A&P heir Huntington Hartford. In the 2000s, Brad Cloepfil redesigned 2 Columbus Circle for the Museum of Arts and Design (MAD), which has occupied the building since 2008.

facts.fact: The nine-storey building fills a small block on the south side of Columbus Circle.
facts.quote: 2 Columbus Circle (formerly the Gallery of Modern Art and the New York Cultural Center) is a nine-story building on the south side of Columbus Circle in the Midtown Manhattan neighborhood of New York City. The building fills a small city block bounded by 58th Street, Columbus Circle, Broadway, and Eighth Avenue.

facts.fact: Its reinforced concrete outer walls are load-bearing and carry the concrete floor slabs.
facts.quote: The exterior walls are made of reinforced concrete, which double as load-bearing walls that support the concrete floor slabs inside.

facts.fact: Stone's façade was mostly white Vermont marble slabs, with small windows only at the corners and loggias at the base and top.
facts.quote: The original facade largely consisted of white Vermont marble slabs, with small windows only at the corner of the building, as well as loggias at the base and top of the building.

facts.fact: Stone kept the windows as small as possible, and newspapers likened them to portholes.
facts.quote: Stone designed the windows to be as small as possible, and the Times and Herald Tribune likened the windows to portholes.

facts.fact: The base had a loggia of reinforced concrete columns recalling the Doge's Palace.
facts.quote: The base of the building contained a loggia of reinforced concrete columns, evocative of that at the Doge's Palace.

facts.fact: The Gallery of Modern Art opened on 21 March 1964.
facts.quote: The museum opened on March 21, 1964, and suffered financially for several years.

facts.fact: Cloepfil's new façade is 4-inch-thick terracotta panels separated by deep grooves.
facts.quote: The new facade consists of 4-inch-thick (10 cm) terracotta panels separated by deep grooves.

facts.fact: The Güell Pavilions are a group of buildings in Pedralbes, Barcelona, by Antoni Gaudí, built between 1884 and 1887.
facts.quote: The so-called Pavellons Güell, or Güell Pavilions, is a complex of buildings in the neighborhood of Pedralbes, Barcelona, by the Catalan Modernist architect Antoni Gaudí, built between 1884 and 1887.

facts.fact: Gaudí was commissioned to remodel the estate's house and build a boundary wall with gates.
facts.quote: Gaudí was commissioned to remodel the house and build a perimeter wall with gates.

facts.fact: Gaudí proposed an Orientalist design, somewhat reminiscent of Mudéjar art.
facts.quote: Gaudí proposed an Orientalist design, somewhat reminiscent of Mudejar art.

facts.fact: The pavilions are a stable, a riding ring and gatehouses.
facts.quote: The Pavilions consist of a stable, longeing ring and gatehouses.

facts.fact: The stable has a high Catalan vault in a catenary curve, and the square riding ring is topped by a hyperboloid dome and lantern.
facts.quote: The stable is rectangular and roofed with a high Catalan vault adopting a catenary curve; the longeing ring has a square ground-plan, but is surmounted by a hyperboloid dome topped by an ornamental lantern; the gatehouses consist of three small buildings, the central one being polygonal in plan and the others cuboidal.

facts.fact: All the buildings are of brick in shades from red to yellow, covered in coloured glass.
facts.quote: All the buildings are built of brick in a range of shades from red to yellow, and covered in coloured glass; in certain sections prefabricated cement blocks are also used.

facts.fact: The main gate is a wrought-iron dragon with glass eyes, representing Ladon from the myth of the Hesperides.
facts.quote: He planned an ashlar wall with several gates, of which the main gate would be a wrought-iron grille in the shape of a dragon, with glass eyes; it represented Ladon, offspring of Typhus, the dragon that guarded the Garden of the Hesperides, which was overcome by Hercules as one of his twelve labours—an episode that was narrated by Jacint Verdaguer in his poem L'Atlàntida, dedicated to Antonio López y López, first marquis of Comillas, who was Eusebi Güell's brother in law.

facts.fact: They were declared a Monument of National Historic and Artistic Interest in 1969.
facts.quote: In 1969 the Pavellons Güell were declared a Monument of National Historic and Artistic Interest.

facts.fact: Trinity Church stands in Boston's Back Bay and is a parish of the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts.
facts.quote: Trinity Church in the City of Boston, located in the Back Bay neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, is a parish of the Episcopal Diocese of Massachusetts.

facts.fact: After the old church burned in the Great Boston Fire of 1872, the new one was built under Rector Phillips Brooks.
facts.quote: After its former site on Summer Street burned in the Great Boston Fire of 1872, the current church complex was erected under the direction of Rector Phillips Brooks (1835–1893), one of the best-known and most charismatic preachers of his time.

facts.fact: H. H. Richardson designed the church and parish house, built from 1872 to 1877.
facts.quote: The church and parish house were designed by Henry Hobson Richardson and construction took place from 1872 to 1877, when the complex was consecrated.

facts.fact: It is the building that made Richardson's name and is the birthplace and archetype of Richardsonian Romanesque.
facts.quote: Situated on Copley Square in Back Bay, Trinity Church is the building that established Richardson's reputation. It is the birthplace and archetype of the Richardsonian Romanesque style, characterized by a clay roof, polychromy, rough stone, heavy arches, and a massive tower.

facts.fact: The style was soon taken up for public buildings across the US, and the church is built of Dedham granite.
facts.quote: This style was soon adopted for a number of public buildings across the United States. The stone used was Dedham Granite.

facts.fact: Stanford White, then in Richardson's office, designed the main tower in 1872, based on the Old Cathedral of Salamanca.
facts.quote: Stanford White, then working in H.H. Richardson's office, designed the current main tower of the Trinity Church of Boston in 1872, basing it on the romanesque tower of the Old Cathedral of Salamanca (Spain).

facts.fact: Its interior is one of the leading examples of the Arts and Crafts aesthetic in the US, and it was Richardson's first work with Augustus Saint-Gaudens.
facts.quote: The interior of the church is one of the leading examples of the arts and crafts aesthetic in the United States. It was at Trinity that Richardson first worked with Augustus Saint Gaudens, with whom he would work multiple times in the ensuing years.

facts.fact: In 1885 American architects named ten best buildings, and half were Richardson's, Trinity Church among them.
facts.quote: He was well-recognized by his peers; of ten buildings named by American architects as the best in 1885, fully half were his: besides Trinity Church, there were Albany City Hall, Sever Hall at Harvard University, the New York State Capitol in Albany (as a collaboration), and Oakes Ames Memorial Hall in North Easton, Massachusetts.
